43037535.bottom_line: In the 10-year extended follow-up of DECISION-CTO, an initial CTO-PCI strategy did not reduce the composite of death, myocardial infarction, stroke or any revascularization compared with an initial no CTO-PCI strategy, although wide confidence intervals leave both benefit and harm possible.
43037535.design: Open-label, multicenter randomized trial (19 centers in 5 Asian countries) with extended 10-year follow-up; modified intention-to-treat analysis.
43037535.population: 834 patients with chronic total occlusion randomly assigned between March 2010 and October 2016; 804 included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (413 CTO-PCI, 391 no CTO-PCI). Clinical follow-up at 10 years was complete in 688 patients (85.6%), without a significant between-group difference (P = 0.69).
43037535.intervention: Initial strategy of percutaneous coronary intervention of the chronic total occlusion, with guideline-directed medical therapy and PCI of obstructive non-CTO lesions encouraged.
43037535.comparison: Initial strategy of no CTO-PCI, with guideline-directed medical therapy and PCI of obstructive non-CTO lesions encouraged in both groups.
43037535.outcomes: Primary endpoint was the composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, stroke, or any revascularization at 10 years: 134 patients in the CTO-PCI group versus 138 in the no CTO-PCI group (Kaplan-Meier estimates 33.9% vs 37.4%; risk difference -3.5 percentage points; 95% CI -10.4 to 3.3 percentage points; P = 0.32).
key_results: Primary composite endpoint at 10 years: 33.9% (CTO-PCI) vs 37.4% (no CTO-PCI); risk difference -3.5 percentage points (95% CI -10.4 to 3.3); P = 0.32.
Restricted mean event-free survival time at 10 years: 7.52 vs 7.53 years; difference -0.01 years (95% CI -0.54 to 0.52); P = 0.97.
Follow-up completeness at 10 years was 85.6% (688 of 804 patients), with no significant between-group difference (P = 0.69).
strengths: Randomized allocation with an exceptionally long 10-year follow-up horizon for a CTO strategy trial, and high follow-up completeness (85.6%).
Both arms received guideline-directed medical therapy and PCI of non-CTO lesions, isolating the effect of treating the occlusion itself.
Analysis included a restricted mean event-free survival time estimate, which is less dependent on proportional hazards than a hazard ratio over a decade of follow-up.
limitations: The confidence interval for the primary risk difference (-10.4 to 3.3 percentage points) is wide, so a clinically meaningful benefit or harm cannot be excluded; the authors state this precludes definitive conclusions.
Open-label design, and any revascularization is part of the composite primary endpoint, which can be influenced by unblinded clinicians and patients.

The original trial enrolled fewer patients than planned relative to its design assumptions and the extended analysis is not a fresh randomization, so the 10-year comparison is underpowered for hard endpoints such as mortality.
Conducted entirely at Asian centers between 2010 and 2016, so generalizability to contemporary CTO technique, equipment and other populations is uncertain.
Crossover and the modified intention-to-treat analysis set (804 of 834 randomized) may dilute the comparison; funding source not reported in the abstract.
43037535.practice_implications: Ten-year data continue to provide no evidence that opening a chronic total occlusion as an initial strategy improves hard outcomes over medical therapy with non-CTO revascularization, supporting symptom relief rather than event reduction as the main rationale for CTO-PCI; the imprecision of the estimate means the question is not definitively settled.

candidates.title: Acute pulmonary embolism: long-term cause-specific mortality in a Chinese nationwide registry.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Long-term cause-specific mortality after acute pulmonary embolism (PE) remains poorly characterized. This study investigated cumulative mortality, temporal changes in causes of death, and associated factors in a national registry.
METHODS: This registry-based cohort study consecutively enrolled 66 192 acute PE patients from 3223 Chest Pain Centres across China (2018-2023) (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04014972). Mortality was ascertained through national registry linkage. Cumulative incidence functions estimated temporal mortality patterns, while Fine-Gray models exploratorily examined factors associated with cause-specific mortality.
RESULTS: At 60 months, cumulative all-cause mortality was 22.41% (95% confidence interval [CI] 21.92-22.91), comprising cardiovascular (CV) (11.84%, 95% CI 11.46-12.23) and non-CV mortality (10.57%, 95% CI 10.22-10.92). Causes of death varied over time: acute PE and ischaemic heart disease (IHD) predominated initially, malignancy peaked at 1-3 months, and IHD was the largest named cause in each interval beyond 12 months. Among CV deaths, IHD was the predominant cause (35.7%); malignancy (43.3%) and chronic pulmonary disease (24.6%) predominated among non-CV deaths. Men had higher cumulative CV and non-CV mortality than women; while women only had a higher proportion of CV causes among deaths. All-cause mortality increased with age (from 11.52% at <55 to 38.51% at ≥75 years); acute PE/malignancy dominated in younger patients, while CV/pulmonary disease prevailed in older ones. Exploratory analyses identified age, Western China residence, and vital signs as factors associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients hospitalised with acute PE, 5-year cumulative mortality was 22.4%, and nearly half of deaths were from non-CV causes. Shifting mortality patterns highlight the need to evaluate risk-adapted long-term follow-up strategies.

candidates.title: Sex-Related Differences in Patients Undergoing Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair for Primary Mitral Regurgitation: PRIME-MR Registry Insights.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Sex-related differences have been previously explored in patients with mitral regurgitation (MR) undergoing surgery as well as those with secondary MR treated with transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER).
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate sex-related differences in baseline characteristics and clinical outcomes in patients undergoing TEER for primary MR.
METHODS: Outcomes of Patients Treated with M-TEER for Primary MR (NCT05332782) is an international, retrospective registry including patients undergoing TEER for primary MR in 27 centers. The primary outcome was a composite of 2-year all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization.
RESULTS: A total of 2,078 patients, including 961 (46.3%) females, were analyzed. Females were older and had fewer comorbidities but presented with a different anatomy and more advanced symptoms. Compared with males, females were more frequently excluded from surgery because of advanced age and frailty. Optimal procedural results were lower in females, with a higher incidence of residual MR ≥2+ (38.5% vs 32.1%; P = 0.0037), and a significantly higher mean transmitral gradient (4.0 vs 3.6 mm Hg; P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier curves showed significantly lower rates of all-cause mortality and cardiovascular mortality in female patients. In contrast, the incidence of the primary composite endpoint, as well as heart failure hospitalization alone, did not differ significantly. After adjusting for comorbidities, females demonstrated lower primary composite endpoint (HR: 0.77; P = 0.009), lower all-cause mortality (HR: 0.62; P < 0.001), and lower cardiovascular mortality (subdistribution HR: 0.53; P = 0.011).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with primary MR, females were older and presented with a different clinical and anatomical profile compared with males. Although optimal procedural results were lower in females, higher survival rates in females vs males suggest that mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair can be a good option regardless of sex.

candidates.title: Lipid-Lowering Strategies in the Era of Early Atherosclerosis Detection: 2026 ACC Scientific Statement: A Report of the American College of Cardiology.
candidates.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) begins early in life, driven in large part by cumulative exposure to low-density lipoprotein cholesterol and other atherogenic lipoproteins. Contemporary evidence from epidemiologic cohorts, genetic studies, imaging studies, and lipid-lowering trials supports a paradigm of earlier identification and more sustained treatment of individuals at increased ASCVD risk. This American College of Cardiology Scientific Statement reviews the rationale for early adoption of lipid-lowering strategies, with emphasis on lifetime lipid burden, inherited and acquired risk enhancers, and the role of subclinical atherosclerosis assessment. Available clinical trial data suggest that greater absolute low-density lipoprotein cholesterol reduction and longer treatment duration can reduce ASCVD events, even though direct evidence remains limited in younger populations at low short-term risk. Atherosclerosis detected by imaging may identify individuals whose ASCVD risk is underestimated by traditional calculators, but optimal strategies for screening, treatment thresholds, safety, adherence, cost-effectiveness, and value require further study. Clinicians should integrate estimated short- and long-term risk, lipid burden, risk enhancers, imaging findings when appropriate, and patient preferences to guide individualized, shared decision making to reduce lifetime ASCVD risk.

candidates.title: Dynamic Risk Assessment of Severe Ventricular Arrhythmia in Patients With Implantable Defibrillators and Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Device shocks are associated with an adverse prognosis in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators. This study aimed to develop and validate a predictive model based on dynamic changes in intracardiac electrograms to assess the risk of polymorphic ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation (VF) events in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillators and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF).
METHODS: Experimental studies were conducted in pigs with HFrEF (N=8) to characterize intracardiac electrogram and surface ECG changes during HF decompensation. Sham-operated animals (N=6) were used as controls. In patients, the study used data from 2 independent cohorts of patients with ICDs. The first cohort included 5089 patients from 50 centers (199 218 tracings), leveraging electrical parameters associated with HFrEF decompensation in the experimental model to train and internally validate a dynamic convolutional neural network model for polymorphic ventricular tachycardia/VF prediction. External validation was performed in a second cohort of 2040 patients from 7 centers (369 845 tracings).
RESULTS: In pigs, HFrEF decompensation was associated with QRS prolongation on surface ECG tracings and reduced bipolar R-wave amplitude in intracardiac electrograms. Hemodynamic and electrical alterations of HFrEF decompensation significantly increased the risk of inducible VF episodes compared with sham-operated controls (87.5% versus 0%, respectively; P<0.001). In a clinical setting, a convolutional neural network-derived model predicted first VF or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia events by analyzing temporal patterns of R-wave amplitude, QRS duration, and premature ventricular complex burden. This approach yielded areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.787 (0.753-0.817) for the training cohort and 0.725 (0.709-0.739) for the external validation cohort. Dynamic risk prediction using the convolutional neural network model significantly outperformed static risk assessment based on clinical variables (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve, 0.617 [0.602-0.632]).
CONCLUSIONS: A convolutional neural network-derived model, grounded in the pathophysiology of HFrEF, provides dynamic risk assessment of VF or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia events in patients with implantable cardioverter-defibrillator devices.

To do this, we will assess the discrimination, calibration, and clinical applicability of the models in external and internal validation studies. Population Adults aged 40-74 years without established CVD, in primary prevention settings. Index prognostic model The WHO non-laboratory-based 10-year CVD risk prediction model, which estimates future cardiovascular risk using demographic and clinical predictors without requiring laboratory measurements. Comparator No comparator is required, as this review evaluates the external predictive performance of the WHO non-laboratory-based 10-year CVD risk prediction model rather than comparing different prediction models. Outcomes Calibration and discrimination of 10-year CVD risk. Timing Risk prediction is performed at baseline using the WHO non-laboratory-based model, with outcomes predicted over a 10-year time horizon. Setting Primary prevention and routine care settings, including resource-limited contexts where laboratory-based cardiovascular risk assessment is not readily available.

candidates.title: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection: implications for women's health, clinical care, and future research.
candidates.abstract: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection (SCAD) is an increasingly recognised cause of acute coronary syndromes, characterised by spontaneous separation of the layers of the coronary arterial wall. It predominantly affects younger women, and recent registry and imaging studies indicate that SCAD is more common than previously appreciated, challenging its historical classification as a rare condition. Clinically, SCAD is associated with a substantial early risk of adverse events, particularly in the first weeks after the index dissection. Given the high frequency of spontaneous healing, conservative management is preferred for most patients, whereas revascularisation is generally reserved for ongoing ischaemia or haemodynamic compromise. However, evidence to guide both pharmacological and interventional management remains scarce. This Review summarises current evidence on SCAD epidemiology, underlying mechanisms including genetic susceptibility, diagnostic approaches, management principles, implications for reproductive and women's health, and research priorities to improve outcomes for affected patients.

candidates.title: Implementation Feasibility and Clinical Utility of Phenomapping in Dilated and Hypokinetic Non-dilated Non-ischemic Cardiomyopathy.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Despite phenotypic heterogeneity, the management of idiopathic non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (NICM) remains generalized and dominantly guided by left ventricular (LV) ejection fraction (EF) and NYHA class. We aimed to develop a point-of-service phenomapping pathway for dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) and hypokinetic non-dilated cardiomyopathy (HNDC) at time of CMR imaging leveraging the integration of i) patient self-reported health status, ii) imaging phenotype, and the iii) electronic health record (EHR).
METHODS AND RESULTS: 1,355 patients (752 DCM and 603 HNDC) were followed for the composite MACE outcome of mortality, heart failure hospitalization or ventricular arrhythmia. K-means clustering was independently applied to DCM and HNDC derivation cohorts using 55 routinely captured features (16 patient-reported health variables, 19 CMR-derived, 14 EHR-derived, and 6 combined features), identifying three phenogroups in each cohort. Over a median of 3.9 and 3.7 years, 145 DCM patients (22%) and 65 HNDC patients (13%), respectively, experienced MACE. Adjusting for age, sex, NYHA class, and LV EF, phenogroup membership was independently associated with future outcomes. In DCM, the adjusted HR (95% CI) of phenogroups 2 and 3 versus Phenogroup 1 were 2.8 (1.6-4.8) and 3.5 (1.9-6.5), respectively (p<0.001 for both). In HNDC, Phenogroup 3 demonstrated an adjusted HR of 4.2 (1.7-10.2; p=0.001) versus Phenogroup 1. Prospective phenogroup assignment was enabled by a decision tree-classifier and validated in a temporal hold-out cohort.
CONCLUSION: Phenomapping delivers incremental value to LVEF and NYHA for identification of high-risk NICM patients. These findings support value from standardized, point-of-service data integration for the delivery of phenomics-driven personalized care.

candidates.title: Blood pressure and arterial stiffness in the pathway between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk: exploratory mediation analysis in middle-aged and older adult men.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: The extent to which blood pressure (BP) and arterial stiffness mediate the association between long-term PM2.5 exposure and cardiovascular risk, and whether individuals with metabolic impairment are more susceptible, remain unclear.
METHODS: Within the "Risk of Cardiovascular diseases and abdominal aortic Aneurysms in Varese" (RoCAV) cohort, we retained 2119 men aged 50-75 and free of coronary heart disease (CHD) and stroke at baseline; carotid-femoral Pulse Wave Velocity (cfPWV) was measured in a subset of 1015 using an automated oscillometer. Exposure was the 12-month mean PM2.5 concentration before baseline (EXPANSE models); outcome was incident major acute CHD or stroke (MACE), fatal or non-fatal. We estimated the mediating contribution of BP and cfPWV through Marginal Structural Models and Aalen survival models, with individual- and area-level confounders.
RESULTS: In a median follow-up of 7.6 years, 178 MACE events occurred (rate=1155 per 100,000 person-years), and 76 (1086/100,000 p-y) in the cfPWV subset. Systolic BP, mean BP, brachial pulse pressure and cfPWV were highest in the most exposed. Each 1-µg/m3 increase in PM2.5 was associated with 151 (95%CI:21-282) additional MACE events per 100,000 p-y, of which 48 (95%CI:17-79) were mediated by cfPWV (mediated proportion: 32%). Systolic BP and brachial pulse pressure each mediated about 16% of the PM2.5-associated risk. The cfPWV-mediated effect was enhanced in men with impaired glucose (96;95%CI:38-155) and elevated LDL-cholesterol (88;95%CI:28-147).
CONCLUSIONS: Large-artery stiffness substantially contributes to the MACE burden associated with chronic PM2.5 exposure, especially in men with metabolic impairment. Monitoring cfPWV may help incorporate environmental risk into cardiovascular prevention.

candidates.title: Discontinuation of Anticoagulation in Patients at Relatively High Risk of Stroke After Successful Catheter Ablation for Atrial Fibrillation: A Nationwide Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Oral anticoagulant (OAC) discontinuation after atrial fibrillation (AF) ablation may be feasible in selected patients; however, outcomes in those at high stroke risk remain unclear.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate associations between OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after ablation and thromboembolic or bleeding events across CHA2DS2-VA risk strata.
METHODS: Patients without AF recurrence within 12 months of catheter ablation and with CHA2DS2-VA scores ≥2 were identified from the Korean National Health Insurance Service database and classified as OAC continuers or discontinuers based on prescription coverage at the 12-month landmark. The primary outcome was a composite of stroke or systemic embolism and major bleeding. Doubly robust estimation combined overlap weighting with covariate-adjusted Cox regression, stratified by CHA2DS2-VA score (2-4 and ≥5).
RESULTS: Among 3,637 patients (mean age: 60.8 ± 9.7 years, 27.1% female, mean CHA2DS2-VA 3.2 ± 1.3), discontinuation in those with scores of 2-4 (n = 3,054) was associated with lower risks of the composite event (HR: 0.61; 95% CI: 0.38-0.96) and major bleeding (HR: 0.51; 95% CI: 0.29-0.90), without increased stroke or systemic embolism (HR: 0.73; 95% CI: 0.34-1.58). In those with scores ≥5 (n = 583), discontinuation was not significantly associated with any outcome, and tests for interaction were not significant (all P > 0.46).
CONCLUSIONS: In this nationwide cohort, OAC discontinuation beyond 1 year after AF ablation was associated with decreased bleeding risk without a corresponding increase in thromboembolic events among patients with CHA2DS2-VA score 2 to 4.

candidates.title: Epigenetic DNA Methylation Patterns Stratify Heart Failure Phenotypes and Predict Clinical Outcome.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Environmental and lifestyle exposures contribute substantially to heart failure (HF) development and progression. DNA methylation integrates cumulative environmental exposures and may provide insight into biological pathways and risk stratification across HF phenotypes.
OBJECTIVES: The aim of this study was to identify phenotype-specific DNA methylation patterns across HF subtypes and evaluate their association with clinical outcomes.
METHODS: Individuals with symptomatic HF (universal definition stage C or D; HF with preserved ejection fraction, HF with mildly reduced ejection fraction, and heart failure with reduced ejection fraction [HFrEF]) from the MyoVasc (An Epidemiological Cohort Study to Investigate the Development and Progression of Heart Failure and the Interaction With Vascular Disease) cohort (N = 3,289) and individuals without cardiovascular disease from the population-based GHS (Gutenberg Health Study) (N = 18,700) were analyzed. Genome-wide DNA methylation from whole blood was measured using the Illumina Infinium MethylationEPIC array. Phenotype-specific DNA methylation scores were derived using penalized regression models adjusted for cardiovascular risk factors.
RESULTS: Distinct and partially overlapping DNA methylation patterns were identified across HF phenotypes, with limited overlap at the CpG level but substantial convergence at the gene level. Phenotype-specific methylation scores discriminated patients with HF from control subjects with high accuracy (area under the curve: 0.97-0.98). Methylation signatures in HF with preserved ejection fraction were associated predominantly with metabolic and inflammatory markers, whereas HFrEF signatures were more strongly linked to markers of myocardial injury and vascular disease. All methylation scores were independently associated with composite of cardiac death or hospitalization for worsening HF and all-cause mortality, with the strongest association observed for the HFrEF score (HR: ∼1.7 per SD).
CONCLUSIONS: Symptomatic HF phenotypes are characterized by distinct and shared DNA methylation signatures. These epigenetic profiles reflect relevant biological pathways and are associated with adverse clinical outcomes, supporting their potential utility in HF risk stratification and precision medicine.

candidates.title: Current Patterns and Best Practices for Prescribing Novel Heart Failure Medications in Children: A Science Advisory From the American Heart Association.
candidates.abstract: Robust evidence from randomized controlled trials of novel heart failure medications in adults has demonstrated improved quality of life, reduced hospitalizations, and decreased mortality, informing current treatment guidelines. In contrast, data supporting the clinical benefits of newer heart failure therapies in children remain limited. To assess contemporary prescribing practices and clinician perspectives, we surveyed pediatric heart failure physicians across the United States and Canada regarding the use of angiotensin receptor-neprilysin inhibitors, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, and iron replacement therapy in children. We also reviewed the existing pediatric literature and summarized reported side effects, dosing experience, and practical guidance for the use of these therapies in the absence of rigorous evidence.
authors: American Heart Association Council on Lifelong Congenital Heart Disease and Heart Health in the Young, Pediatric Heart Failure and Transplantation Committee; Council on Clinical Cardiology; and Council on Cardiovascular and Stroke Nursing

candidates.title: Incidence, Risk Factors and Natural History of Atrial Arrhythmias in Patients With Systemic Right Ventricle.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The incidence and risk factors for atrial arrhythmia (AA; atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter) in adults with systemic right ventricle (sRV), specifically congenitally corrected transposition of the great arteries and dextro-transposition of the great arteries palliated with atrial switch procedures, are not well understood. This study aims to better define these risks.
METHODS: Adults with sRV presenting to Mayo Clinic between 2000 and 2022 were identified. Their clinical characteristics, electrocardiographic, and echocardiographic parameters at the time of first presentation were recorded. The incidence of sustained AA (>30 seconds) during follow-up was documented. Cox regression analysis was used to identify associations of incident atrial fibrillation/atrial flutter and mortality during follow-up.
RESULTS: Among 447 patients with sRV (median age, 33.1 [24.6-42.8], 55.9% male, 247 cm3-TGA; 200 dextro-transposition of the great arteries postatrial switch), AA was present at first visit in 113 (25.3%). Out of the remaining 334 patients, new-onset AA occurred in 125 (37.4%) patients during a median follow-up of 11.1 years (interquartile range, 3.6-19.3). Isolated atrial fibrillation was observed in 89 (37.4%), isolated atrial flutter in 76 (31.9%), and both atrial fibrillation and atrial flutter in 73 (30.7%) patients. In multivariable analysis, the risk factors for incident AA included age (hazard ratio, 1.04 [1.03-1.06]; P<0.001), d-TGA (hazard ratio, 1.96 [1.00-3.85]; P=0.05), and QRS duration (hazard ratio, 1.01 [1.00-1.02]; P=0.02). AA was associated with hospitalization for heart failure in 19% of patients. Among those treated with anti-arrhythmic drugs and ablation, recurrence occurred in over 50% of patients. AA was not an independent predictor of mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: AA occurred in more than half of this cohort with sRV, with risk increasing significantly after the third decade of life. Advancing age, dextro-transposition of the great arteries, and prolonged QRS duration were associated with increased risk of AA. Close monitoring for AA and early interventions are warranted in all adults with sRV.

candidates.title: Night shift work and subclinical cardiac remodelling: a multi-omic CMR study in 42 671 individuals.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Whether frequent night-shift work is associated with a distinct subclinical cardiac phenotype and accompanying molecular alterations remains uncertain.
METHODS AND RESULTS: We analysed 42 671 UK Biobank participants without baseline cardiovascular disease who underwent cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR). Night-shift frequency was classified into four categories, and 15 CMR measures were assessed using multivariable regression. Compared with day workers, frequent night-shift workers showed greater left ventricular global wall thickness [standardized β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.050-0.135; false discovery rate (FDR) < 0.001] and left ventricular mass-to-volume ratio (β = 0.072, 95% CI 0.021-0.123; FDR = 0.019), with lower left ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular end-diastolic volume index, right ventricular stroke volume index, and maximal right atrial volume index (all FDR < 0.05). Left ventricular global circumferential strain was less favourable (β = 0.092, 95% CI 0.040-0.144; FDR = 0.002), whereas left ventricular ejection fraction and global longitudinal strain were not significantly associated. Proteomic (n = 4889) and metabolomic (n = 42 671) analyses identified exploratory inflammatory, vascular, and lipid-related correlates. Mediation analyses identified FDR-significant indirect-effect estimates involving left ventricular end-diastolic volume index for three proteins and four metabolites. Two-sample Mendelian randomization identified associations between selected molecular features and CMR traits, although directions were not uniformly concordant with the observational estimates.
CONCLUSION: Frequent night shift work was associated with greater concentric left ventricular geometry, lower cardiac chamber volumes, and less favourable circumferential strain, together with inflammatory and lipid-related molecular correlates. Prospective studies are required to determine temporal relationships and long-term clinical relevance.

candidates.title: Residual Peridevice Leak at 45-Day Transesophageal Echocardiogram After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion.
Anemia and Iron Status in Pregnant and Postpartum Women With Acute Heart Failure.
candidates.abstract:
IMPORTANCE: In low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), iron-deficient anemia is highly prevalent and may compound the cardiovascular stress of pregnancy, yet its contribution to maternal acute heart failure (AHF) is poorly understood.
OBJECTIVES: To investigate the association of maternal anemia and iron status with AHF in pregnancy and post partum in India.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This multicenter, unmatched, prospective case-control study recruited participants from 10 hospitals across 4 Indian states from February 2019 to November 2024. Incident cases were pregnant or postpartum women with clinically diagnosed AHF. Controls were women without history or symptoms of heart disease within 48 hours post partum. Data were analyzed from March 2025 to April 2026.
EXPOSURES: Maternal anemia and iron status. Blood samples collected at recruitment were analyzed for hemoglobin, ferritin, transferrin saturation, soluble transferrin receptor, and hepcidin.
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The outcome of interest was AHF, defined using clinical criteria. Multivariable logistic regression models assessed associations of iron status and anemia with AHF, adjusting for potential confounders, including hypertensive disorders of pregnancy. Subgroup analyses were performed in women with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. The discriminatory capacity of a model including anemia present before AFH onset vs a model with established risk factors only was examined using receiver operating characteristic curves.
RESULTS: Among 532 women with clinically diagnosed AHF (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-29] years) and 1091 controls (median [IQR] age, 25 [21-28] years), moderate and severe anemia were associated with 1.5-fold (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 1.52; 95% CI, 1.13-2.05) and 5-fold (aOR, 5.06; 95% CI, 3.02-8.48) increased odds of AHF, respectively, compared with women without anemia. Higher soluble transferrin receptor levels (aOR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.31-1.57) and the lowest hepcidin quintile (aOR, 2.65; 95% CI, 1.69-4.14), both indicative of iron deficiency, were independently associated with AHF. These associations persisted after adjusting for hypertensive disorders of pregnancy and after excluding women with preexisting cardiac conditions, and they were consistent in subgroups with echocardiographic abnormalities and peripartum cardiomyopathy. Adding anemia to established risk factors improved model discrimination for identifying AHF risk, increasing the AUC from 78% (95% CI, 76%-81%) to 83% (95% CI, 80%-85%) (P < .001).
CONCLUSION AND RELEVANCE: This case-control study found that maternal anemia and iron deficiency were independently associated with AHF during pregnancy and post partum. Further studies are needed to determine whether preventing or treating iron deficiency and anemia can reduce AHF risk and improve maternal outcomes.

candidates.title: Prognostic Value of Longitudinal Echo-Dynamic Assessment in Patients with Cardiogenic Shock A multi-center prospective study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: In cardiogenic shock (CS), early hemodynamic changes are associated with in-hospital outcomes, but evidence on non-invasive assessment is limited. We evaluated the prognostic value of a comprehensive non-invasive hemodynamic assessment by echocardiography ("echo-dynamics") at presentation and 48 hours in CS.
METHODS: Consecutive CS patients at four Cardiac Intensive Care Units were prospectively enrolled. Echo-dynamics were obtained at baseline and 48 hours, including stroke volume index (SVi), cardiac index (CI), cardiac power output (CPO), estimated left atrial pressure (E/e'), systolic pulmonary arterial pressure (eSPAP) and right atrial pressure. The primary outcome was a composite of in-hospital mortality, left ventricular assist device implantation or heart transplantation.
RESULTS: Among 457 patients (37.9% acute myocardial infarction-CS, 42.9% SCAI CS stage ≥C, 28% mean ejection fraction), the primary outcome occurred in 30.0%. Each echo-dynamic parameter was associated with the outcome at both time points after adjustment for age, sex, CS etiology and severity. Changes from baseline to 48 hours showed a stepwise risk increase across improving, worsening, or persistently abnormal trajectories (p-trend<0.01). In fully adjusted models, baseline CPO<0.6 W (adj-OR 2.05, 95%CI 1.29-3.26) and eSPAP ≥35 mmHg (adj-OR 2.45, 95%CI 1.44-4.15) were associated with outcomes; at 48 hours, CPO<0.6 W (adj-OR 2.70, 95%CI 1.57-4.66), increased E/e' (adj-OR 1.86, 95%CI 1.09-3.15) and eSPAP ≥35 mmHg (adj-OR 1.90, 95%CI 1.12-3.22) remained independently associated. Results were consistent when adjusting for SCAI stage.
CONCLUSIONS: In CS, longitudinal echo-dynamic assessment identifies distinct trajectories with prognostic implications. Persistently low cardiac power, and elevated filling and pulmonary pressures showed the strongest association with adverse outcomes.

candidates.title: Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Super-High-Pressure Noncompliant Balloons for Treatment of Calcified Coronary Lesions: The VICTORY Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Although calcified coronary lesions are associated with poor outcomes after percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI), randomized data guiding lesion preparation are limited. Small studies suggest potential benefits of super-high-pressure noncompliant balloons (SH-NCB); however, they have not been directly compared with intravascular lithotripsy (IVL).
OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to conduct a randomized comparison of SH-NCBs vs IVL in calcified lesions.
METHODS: In this open-label, randomized controlled, noninferiority trial with blinded outcomes assessment (ie, the PROBE design), patients aged ≥18 years with calcified coronary lesions were randomly assigned (1:1) to undergo lesion preparation with SH-NCBs or IVL before PCI with drug-eluting stents. All patients were required to undergo optical coherence tomography (OCT). The primary endpoint was final stent expansion (%) according to OCT. Secondary endpoints included procedural success, strategy success, target vessel failure, stent expansion <80%, and safety outcomes (eg, coronary perforation).
RESULTS: Between December 21, 2022, and August 11, 2025, a total of 278 patients underwent the randomly assigned study procedure using plaque modification with SH-NCBs or IVL before stent implantation. The majority of patients (68%) had severe calcium based on an OCT Fujino score ≥4. Study procedures involving IVL tended to be longer and require more auxiliary devices compared with SH-NCBs. The median pressure applied with SH-NCBs compared with IVL was 40 atmospheres vs 6 atmospheres. Regarding the primary endpoint of stent expansion, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL (85% vs 84%; Pnoninferiority < 0.0001). The results were consistent across all subgroups, including calcium severity. Use of SH-NCBs, compared with IVL, resulted in similar rates of procedural and strategy success. Safety outcomes, specifically coronary perforations, did not differ between the 2 groups. At 30 days' follow-up, target vessel failure events (including cardiac death, target vessel revascularization, or myocardial infarction) occurred in 4 (2.8%) patients in the SH-NCB group and in 8 (5.7%) patients in the IVL group (HR: 0.50; 95% CI: 0.15 to 1.66; P = 0.26).
CONCLUSIONS: In calcified coronary lesions, SH-NCBs were noninferior to IVL for stent expansion and exhibited a comparable safety profile in experienced operators using intravascular imaging. (Value of IVL Compared To OPN Non-Compliant Balloons for Treatment of Refractory Coronary Lesions [VICTORY]; NCT05346068).

candidates.title: Exploring the upper spectrum of physiological cardiac remodelling in Olympic athletes: insights from a CMR study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) is essential for distinguishing physiological from pathological remodelling in athletes. However, cardiovascular screening protocols vary across studies, leaving uncertainty regarding the true upper limits of physiological adaptation.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to characterise the full spectrum of cardiac remodelling in Olympic athletes and to describe CMR-derived upper limits of cardiac remodelling according to sport category and sex.
METHODS: Olympic athletes with negative comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation underwent voluntary non-contrast CMR. Left and right ventricular volumes, mass, and ejection fraction (EF) were quantified. Cardiac parameters were analysed according to the ESC sport classification and sex. Cluster analysis was performed to identify patterns of cardiac remodelling independently of sport category.
RESULTS: A total of 320 athletes (age 26±5 years, 57% male; 13% skill sports, 19% power, 28% mixed, 40% endurance, 97% Caucasians) were included. Endurance athletes had the largest biventricular volumes and LV mass (all p-values <0.001), with no differences in EF across sport categories. Maximal interventricular septal thickness did not exceed 13 mm in males or 11 mm in females. Only 1% and 2% of athletes had LV or RV EF <50%, respectively, predominantly cyclists. Cluster analysis identified two phenotypes reflecting lower and higher degrees of remodelling, with substantial overlap across sport categories. The sex and sport categories were independently associated with the high-remodelling phenotype.
CONCLUSION: CMR-derived cardiac adaptation in predominantly Caucasian, Olympic athletes varies according to sport category, with endurance athletes demonstrating the most pronounced remodelling. Maximal physiological LV wall thickness was 13 mm in males and 11 mm in females in this cohort, whereas LV EF <50% was uncommon despite marked cardiac remodelling. Finally, the overlap across sport categories and the identification of distinct remodelling phenotypes suggest that cardiac adaptation reflects a continuum rather than discrete sport-specific patterns.

candidates.title: Prognostic Value of Left Ventricular Kinetic Energy Assessed by 4D Flow CMR in Dilated Cardiomyopathy: A Prospective Multicenter Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Alterations in left ventricular intracavitary hemodynamics can occur early in the course of nonischemic dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM). However, the association between 4-dimensional (4D) flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters and adverse outcomes in patients with DCM remains unclear. We aimed to evaluate whether 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance parameters can predict adverse outcomes in patients with DCM.
METHODS: In this multicenter prospective cohort study, 675 adult patients with DCM (mean age, 56 years; 399 men) from 3 medical centers and 80 age- and sex-matched healthy controls underwent 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance. Left ventricular flow components and kinetic energy parameters were quantified. The primary end point was a composite of heart failure events, including heart failure-related death, unplanned heart failure hospitalization, or cardiac transplantation.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 42 months, 58 patients (8.6%) experienced the primary end point. Compared with controls, patients with DCM exhibited reduced peak systolic kinetic energy normalized to EDV (KEiEDV) and peak E-wave KEiEDV; these differences were more pronounced in those who developed the primary end point. In univariable Cox regression, direct flow, residual volume, peak systolic KEiEDV, and peak E-wave KEiEDV were significant predictors of the primary end point (all P<0.05). After adjustment for left ventricular ejection fraction, NT-proBNP (N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide), extracellular volume fraction, extent of late gadolinium enhancement, peak systolic KEiEDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.39 [95% CI, 0.28-0.53]), and peak E-wave KEiEDV (adjusted hazard ratio, 0.35 [95% CI, 0.26-0.48]) remained independently associated with the primary end point (both P<0.001). Furthermore, these 2 kinetic energy parameters provided incremental prognostic value beyond clinical markers and conventional imaging markers for predicting the primary end point.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with DCM, decreased peak systolic KEiEDV and peak E-wave KEiEDV, as measured by 4D flow cardiac magnetic resonance, are independently associated with poor prognosis and provide incremental prognostic value for risk stratification beyond clinical and conventional imaging markers.

candidates.title: Biological Aging Associates With Preeclampsia and Gestational Hypertension.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Biological aging is a fundamental driver of chronic disease, yet its role in the cause of preeclampsia and gestational hypertension remains poorly defined.
METHODS: We used a multimodal framework that triangulated genetic, epidemiological, and experimental approaches to assess the associations of biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension. Publicly available human and mouse transcriptomic data were analyzed to identify shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures, while the potential of nicotinic acid to alleviate aging- and preeclampsia-related features was further evaluated in experimental models.
RESULTS: Two-sample Mendelian randomization demonstrated that biological age acceleration was associated with higher odds of preeclampsia (odds ratio, 1.55 [95% CI, 1.22-1.96]; P=2.67×10-4) and gestational hypertension (odds ratio, 1.56 [95% CI, 1.12-2.19]; P=0.009), while positive genetic correlations were also observed for both outcomes. In the nested case-control study, higher early pregnancy biological age acceleration was consistently associated with preeclampsia risk in both primary (odds ratio, 1.16 [95% CI, 1.01-1.35]; P=0.047) and sensitivity (odds ratio, 1.14 [95% CI, 1.03-1.29]; P=0.042) analyses, with the associations persisting after covariate adjustment and exclusion of systolic blood pressure from biological age acceleration calculation. Mouse models exhibited preeclampsia-like features accompanied by concordant alterations in biological age-related biomarkers and telomere dysfunction. These changes were partially attenuated by nicotinic acid treatment, whereas placental organoids showed limited growth responses to nicotinic acid. Complementing these phenotypic observations, transcriptomic analyses identified shared aging- and preeclampsia-associated signatures across human and mouse data sets.
CONCLUSIONS: Convergent evidence links biological aging with preeclampsia and gestational hypertension, particularly biological age acceleration with preeclampsia. Experimental findings provide complementary context but do not establish a specific mechanism or therapeutic role for nicotinic acid.

candidates.title: Ventricular Morphology and Atrioventricular Valve Regurgitation in Adults Post-Fontan: Associations With Exercise Hemodynamics.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Right ventricular (RV) dominance and atrioventricular valve regurgitation (AVVR) are associated with adverse outcomes post-Fontan palliation, but their underlying hemodynamic correlates, particularly during exercise, remain incompletely characterized.
METHODS: In this cross-sectional cohort, exercise hemodynamics by ventricular morphology and AVVR severity were assessed invasively (supine exercise catheterization) in 108 individuals and semi-invasively (semisupine exercise with echocardiography and peripheral venous pressure) in 108.
RESULTS: Age of the invasive cohort was 32.1 (25.6-37.2) years; 41 had RV dominance, 19 had moderate or severe AVVR, and 16 had both. Resting and peak mean pulmonary artery pressure and pulmonary artery wedge pressure were similar across ventricular morphologies and AVVR severity. However, RV dominance was associated with lower systemic (systemic blood flow, 67% [22-93] versus 86% [63-105] predicted; P=0.006) and pulmonary (pulmonary blood flow, 57% [33-75] versus 72% [61-89] predicted; P<0.001) cardiac output responses to exercise and steeper Δpulmonary artery pressure/Δpulmonary blood flow, (4.3 [2.6-10.6] versus 3.0 [1.7-4.8] mm Hg/L per minute; P=0.004). Patients with moderate or severe AVVR showed a similar pattern, with lower systemic blood flow (64% [19-92] versus 77% [57-101], P=0.10) and pulmonary blood flow (57% [36-74] versus 70% [55-88] predicted, P=0.03) responses. Findings were replicated in the semi-invasive cohort, where RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR were associated with lower peak systemic blood flow and higher Δperipheral venous pressure/Δ systemic blood flow, despite similar peak peripheral venous pressure.
CONCLUSIONS: Resting and exertional pulmonary artery wedge pressure, pulmonary artery pressure, and peripheral venous pressure are unrelated to ventricular morphology and AVVR severity. Conversely, impaired flow augmentation and steeper pressure-flow relationships during exercise were associated with RV dominance and moderate or severe AVVR, emphasizing the role of dynamic provocation to unmask occult cardiovascular reserve limitations.

candidates.title: Evaluation of the ESC Guideline based risk stratification of syncope patients in the emergency department A post-hoc analysis of the SYNERGY-trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Syncope accounts for approximately 1% of all emergency department(ED) visits. With 1-year mortality rates reaching up to 33% in certain arrhythmogenic aetiologies, adequate assessment in the ED is imperative. The risk stratification as described in the 2018 European Society of Cardiology(ESC) guidelines on syncope is widely used in clinical practice, but has never been validated. We therefore aimed to determine the ability to identify cardiac syncope of the composite guideline-based RISC-score, and investigate the association of individual risk-features and cardiac aetiology.
METHODS: 520 patients presenting with syncope to the ED of five Dutch hospitals were included. Adjudicated diagnoses were established by a multidisciplinary expert-panel following one-year of critical follow-up. ED-documentation was analyzed for the presence of guideline risk-features. Overall discriminative ability of the guideline-based RISC-score was evaluated using receiver-operating-characteristic(ROC) curve-analysis. Uni- and multivariate logistic regression analyses were performed to assess the predictive ability of the individual risk-features.
RESULTS: 50 patients(9.6%) were adjudicated with a cardiac aetiology of syncope. The RISC-score demonstrated excellent discriminative ability with an area-under-the-curve(AUC) of 0.928. The guideline based cut-off threshold of 2 points yielded a sensitivity of 96.0%, a specificity of 78.5%, a positive predictive value of 33.2% and a negative predictive value of 99.5%. Multivariate regression analysis identified age, no warning-symptoms, angina pectoris, unevaluated systolic murmur, atrial fibrillation, syncope during exertion and bifascicular-block as independent predictors of cardiac syncope.
CONCLUSION: The ESC-guideline based RISC-score can be reliably and safely used for excluding a cardiac aetiology of syncope in patients in the ED.

candidates.title: Venous Vascular Closure System Versus Conventional Figure of Eight Suture Following Single Shot Device Pulmonary Vein Isolation: The VASC-AF Study.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: Optimization of femoral venous access management has become increasingly important as catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation (AF) continues to evolve towards greater safety with accelerated recovery pathways. We evaluated the efficacy and safety of a bioabsorbable venous vascular closure system (VCS) compared with a conventional figure-of-eight (F8) suture and manual compression following contemporary single-shot pulmonary vein isolation (PVI).
METHODS AND RESULTS: VASC-AF was a prospective, multicentre, randomized controlled trial performed at three German electrophysiology centres. One hundred consecutive patients undergoing single-shot PVI were randomized in a 1:1 ratio to femoral venous closure using the VASCADE MVP VCS; (n=50) or conventional F8 suture (n=50). The primary efficacy endpoint was time to ambulation. The primary safety endpoint comprised major periprocedural adverse events requiring medical intervention before hospital discharge.Baseline characteristics and procedural variables were comparable between study groups. Median time to ambulation was significantly shorter following vascular closure with VCS compared with F8 sutures (120 [120-150] vs. 180 [180-240] min; P=0.015). Likewise, time to haemostasis (0.5 [0.5-2] vs. 1 [1-2] min; P=0.021) and time to discharge eligibility (2.5 [2.1-3.0] vs. 4.0 [3.0-5.0] h; P=0.019) were significantly reduced.Major adverse events occurred infrequently and did not differ significantly between groups. In contrast, vascular closure using VCS significantly reduced minor vascular access complications (6% vs. 26%; P=0.006), groin pain, and patient discomfort while improving overall post-procedural satisfaction.
CONCLUSION: Among patients undergoing contemporary single-shot AF ablation, use of a bioabsorbable VCS significantly accelerated post-procedural recovery while maintaining a comparable major safety profile. Reduced access-site complications and improved patient-reported outcomes support VCS as an important component of enhanced recovery pathways following AF ablation especially in an ambulatory or Same-Day Discharge setting.

candidates.title: Controversy: Adjunctive ablation lesions are needed beyond pulmonary vein isolation in treating persistent atrial fibrillation: Pro and Contra.
candidates.abstract: Catheter ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation remains less effective than for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, despite pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) forming the foundation of both procedures. Ablating beyond the pulmonary veins, including treatment of non-pulmonary vein triggers, posterior wall isolation, linear lesions, vein of Marshall ethanol infusion, isolation of the superior vena cava, coronary sinus or left atrial appendage, and modification of regions identified by fibrosis or low voltage has grown interest. Although observational and mechanistic studies have often been encouraging, randomized trials of empirical adjunctive ablation have produced inconsistent or neutral results. Pulsed field ablation has renewed the debate by facilitating rapid ablation of extra-pulmonary vein tissue. The PIFPAF-PFA trial did not demonstrate a significant reduction in its primary endpoint of atrial tachyarrhythmia recurrence lasting at least 30 seconds with adjunctive posterior wall isolation. However, separation of the recurrence curves and exploratory signals for reduced arrhythmia burden and fewer prolonged episodes raise questions about lesion strategy and the clinical relevance of conventional recurrence definitions. These findings do not establish routine posterior wall isolation, but they illustrate why a neutral binary endpoint may not fully characterize treatment effects on recurrent AF. The controversy now extends beyond whether additional ablation is beneficial to which mechanisms should be targeted, which patients should receive adjunctive lesions, how energy source affects lesion durability and safety, and whether success should be defined by any brief recurrence or by clinically meaningful arrhythmia burden. This article examines the evidence supporting and opposing ablation beyond PVI in persistent AF.

candidates.title: Feasibility and safety of leadless pacemaker implantation via the right internal jugular vein: primary results of the VAMPIRE multicenter prospective study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Leadless pacemakers (LPs) are usually implanted through the femoral vein. The right internal jugular vein (RIJV) approach has emerged as an alternative, but evidence remains limited to retrospective single-centre series.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the feasibility, procedural success, and 30-day safety of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation.
METHODS: The VAMPIRE study (NCT06455566) is a prospective, investigator-initiated, multicenter registry enrolling consecutive patients with a guideline-directed LP indication across 15 tertiary centres in France (May 2024-May 2026). The primary endpoint was major procedure- or system-related complications within 30 days.
RESULTS: Of 294 screened patients, 272 (92.5%) underwent a first-line RIJV approach. The cohort was elderly (median age 79 [73-85] years), predominantly male (63.6%), with high comorbidity burden including atrial fibrillation in 51.5%, chronic kidney disease in 34.9%, and cancer in 22.4%. High-degree atrioventricular block was the primary indication in 84.9%; 65.8% of procedures were performed urgently. Successful LP implantation was achieved in 266 of 272 patients (97.8%; 95% CI 95.3-99.2%), with septal deployment in 94.3%. Median procedure time was 30 [25-40] minutes and median fluoroscopy time 2.5 [1.1-7.0] minutes. Major complications occurred in 6 of 272 patients (2.2%; 95% CI 0.8-4.7%; p<0.001).
CONCLUSION: In this prospective multicenter registry of a first-line RIJV approach for LP implantation, feasibility and procedural success were high, and 30-day major complications rate low. These results support the RIJV route as a safe and broadly applicable access strategy for LP implantation. However, dedicated studies are needed to compare safety versus the femoral approach.

candidates.title: Polarimetric Characterization of CCTA-Defined High-Risk Coronary Plaques: Linking Morphology to Fibrous Matrix Organization and Lipid Burden.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: High-risk plaque (HRP) features on coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) predict future coronary events, yet the microstructural substrate underlying these radiological signatures remains largely unknown. Polarization-sensitive (PS) optical frequency domain imaging (OFDI) quantifies tissue birefringence and depolarization-derived lipid core burden index (LCBI) in vivo. We aimed to investigate the relationship between PS-OFDI-derived polarimetric signals and CCTA-defined HRP features.
METHODS: We retrospectively identified 43 patients from a prospective registry of intracoronary polarimetry with PS-OFDI who had undergone CCTA before hospitalization and subsequently underwent OFDI-guided percutaneous coronary intervention. A total of 70 coronary segments were analyzed. HRP was defined as the presence of ≥2 established CCTA features: positive remodeling, low-attenuation plaque, napkin-ring sign, or spotty calcification. Conventional OFDI metrics and PS-OFDI-derived birefringence and depolarization-derived maximum 4-mm LCBI were evaluated in relation to CCTA-defined HRP. Segment-level comparisons accounted for within-patient clustering, and correlation and discrimination analyses incorporated patient-level bootstrap resampling.
RESULTS: Among the 70 analyzed segments, 28 (40%) exhibited CCTA-defined HRP. HRP segments showed lower birefringence and higher depolarization-derived maximum 4-mm LCBI than non-HRP segments (both P<0.001). Birefringence was inversely correlated with low-attenuation plaque volume (ρ=-0.350 [95% CI, -0.543 to -0.131]), whereas depolarization-derived maximum 4-mm LCBI correlated with maximum lipid arc (ρ=0.480 [95% CI, 0.277-0.635]), lipid length (ρ=0.463 [95% CI, 0.199-0.654]), and minimum fibrous cap thickness (ρ=-0.466 [95% CI, -0.661 to -0.212]). Adding birefringence to conventional OFDI maximum lipid arc provided exploratory evidence of incremental discrimination for CCTA-defined HRP: apparent area under the curve increased from 0.673 to 0.853 (Δ area under the curve, 0.180 [95% CI, 0.049-0.370]), with the corresponding optimism-corrected area under the curves of 0.672 and 0.840.
CONCLUSIONS: PS-OFDI-derived metrics were associated with CCTA-defined HRP features and conventional OFDI lipid parameters. Reduced birefringence in HRP lesions suggests altered collagen organization as a potential microstructural substrate underlying adverse plaque morphology identified by CCTA.

candidates.title: The Electrocardiogram as a Preventive Biomarker: From Conventional Risk Markers to Actionable Artificial Intelligence - A Narrative Review.
candidates.abstract: The electrocardiogram (ECG) is an established tool in cardiovascular prevention, identifying silent arrhythmias, hypertrophy, prior myocardial infarction, conduction disease, and inherited electrical disorders. However, conventional interpretation captures only a fraction of the information embedded in the cardiac electrical signal. Because the ECG is inexpensive, non-invasive, standardized, and already acquired at scale, it provides an attractive substrate for artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening and risk stratification. Deep-learning models can identify latent signatures of ventricular dysfunction, structural heart disease, atrial fibrillation, cardiomyopathy, heart failure, and mortality risk. Importantly, evidence is beginning to extend beyond retrospective validation: prospective implementation studies have increased disease detection, while randomized data suggest that AI-ECG-guided clinical alerts may improve outcomes in selected high-risk populations. Whether such benefits extend to preventive populations remains uncertain. This review examines the preventive role of conventional, ambulatory, and wearable ECGs and distinguishes AI applications for detection, prediction, prognostication, treatment selection, and longitudinal monitoring. We argue that performance metrics alone are insufficient. Preventive value requires a defined target population, calibrated and externally validated predictions, an appropriate confirmatory test, a feasible clinical workflow, and an intervention proven to improve outcomes. The most credible near-term applications are those that triage patients to established diagnostic pathways, such as echocardiography or prolonged rhythm monitoring. The central challenge is therefore to transform accurate AI-ECG predictions into actionable, affordable, scalable, safe, and equitable prevention.

candidates.title: Effectiveness of Bariatric Surgery and Incretin-based Therapies on Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients with Obesity: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies improve cardiometabolic risk factors. However, direct head-to-head comparisons assessing their impact on cardiovascular outcomes remain limited. We performed an exploratory meta-analysis to compare bariatric surgery and pharmacological weight-loss therapies on major clinical outcomes in adults with obesity.
METHODS: A systematic literature search using PubMed and Scopus databases was conducted. Randomized and observational studies comparing bariatric surgery or incretin receptor agonists with controls were included in the analysis. The primary outcomes were all-cause mortality and MACE. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis was conducted across three nodes.
RESULTS: A total of 40 studies, comprising more than 1.9 million patients, were included in the meta-analysis. Compared with control, bariatric surgery was associated with a significant reduction in all evaluated outcomes, including all-cause mortality (HR:0.57, 95%CI:0.51-0.65), MACE (HR:0.54, 95%CI:0.45-0.64), cardiovascular mortality, heart failure hospitalization, myocardial infarction, and stroke. Incretin receptor agonists were also associated with lower all-cause mortality (HR:0.62, 95%CI:0.52-0.74), lower MACE (HR:0.75, 95%CI:0.61-0.92) and reduced heart failure hospitalization. All-cause mortality-representing the most direct and clinically relevant endpoint-did not differ significantly between the two strategies in the exploratory network meta-analysis. Importantly, the network estimates should be cautiously interpreted, given the predominance of observational evidence, substantial heterogeneity, and very low confidence across all comparisons.
CONCLUSION: Bariatric surgery and incretin receptor agonists are associated with substantial reductions in major cardiovascular outcomes in adults with obesity. In head-to-head comparisons, no significant differences were observed in all-cause mortality and stroke. Both strategies provide clinically meaningful benefits.

candidates.title: Long working hours and cardiometabolic multimorbidity progression: a prospective multistate analysis in the UK Biobank.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: The association of long working hours with cardiometabolic disease accumulation remains unclear. Cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) was defined as the coexistence of at least two of the following conditions: type 2 diabetes, ischaemic heart disease and stroke.
METHODS: We studied 269,197 employed UK Biobank participants free of cardiometabolic disease (CMD) at baseline. Weekly working hours were analysed in five categories, with 35-40 h/week as reference. Cox models assessed incident first CMD (FCMD), CMM and all-cause mortality. Multistate models assessed progression from no CMD to FCMD and from FCMD to CMM, with death possible from each state. Models were adjusted for demographic, socioeconomic, occupational and family-history factors. Estimates were pooled across 50 multiply imputed datasets.
RESULTS: Within the disease observation window, 25,190 participants developed FCMD and 2,824 developed CMM. Working ≥55 h/week was associated with FCMD (hazard ratio [HR] 1.117, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.057-1.180). Incident CMM from baseline was associated with 41-48 h/week (1.128, 1.010-1.260) and 49-54 h/week (1.205, 1.042-1.393); the estimate for ≥55 h/week was 1.144 (0.973-1.346). For FCMD-to-CMM progression, the corresponding HR were 1.141 (1.021-1.274), 1.129 (0.976-1.306) and 1.093 (0.929-1.286). Spline analyses supported overall associations with FCMD and incident CMM from baseline (both P<0.001), but not a clear association with FCMD-to-CMM progression (P=0.083).
CONCLUSION: Long working hours were associated with first CMD onset and incident CMM in some working-hour groups; FCMD-to-CMM progression showed no clear increasing gradient. These findings support considering working time in cardiometabolic risk assessment while distinguishing initial disease development from subsequent progression.

candidates.title: Early outcomes of tricuspid valve replacement in patients with tricuspid regurgitation: the Trisol Early Feasibility Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) could lead to a paradigm shift in treating tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and improving patient quality of life.
AIMS: We aimed to report the 30-day outcomes of the Trisol Early Feasibility Study (EFS).
METHODS: The Trisol EFS was a single-arm, multicentre study that enrolled patients with symptomatic ≥severe TR despite optimal medical therapy to undergo TTVR with the Trisol system via transjugular access. The primary safety endpoint was the rate of device-related serious adverse events, including death, myocardial infarction, disabling stroke, life-threatening bleeding, renal failure requiring dialysis, and the need for surgery. The primary performance endpoints included technical and procedural success, while secondary endpoints included echocardiographic as well as functional and quality-of-life measures.
RESULTS: A total of 19 patients, who were treated with a latest-generation Trisol 12-anchor valve, were included from August 2023 to September 2025. The mean age was 75.8 years (range 62 to 91), 78.9% were female, and 78.9% were in New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III or IV. TR was reduced to mild or less in 87.5% of the subjects and moderate or less in 100% of the subjects. The 30-day composite major adverse event rate was 10.5% (2/19) due to one cardiovascular death and one pacemaker implantation. No other complications were observed. NYHA Class significantly improved to Class I/II (87.5%), and the Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved by a mean of 13.6±34.6 points.
CONCLUSIONS: In this early clinical experience, the Trisol TTVR system demonstrated technical feasibility, overall safety, significant TR reduction, and the ability to improve quality of life and functional status in TR patients.

candidates.title: Anterior mitral leaflet modification to prevent left ventricular outflow tract obstruction during transcatheter mitral valve replacement: the PROTECT-LVOT registry.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left ventricular outflow tract (LVOT) obstruction remains the major limitation of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR). Anterior mitral leaflet (AML) modification has emerged as a key preventive strategy, yet real-world data remain limited and residual risk is still unknown.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the outcomes of TMVR with concomitant AML modification across valve-in-mitral annular calcification (ViMAC), valve-in-ring (ViR), and valve-in-valve (ViV) substrates.
METHODS: We established a multicentre retrospective registry of consecutive patients undergoing TMVR with AML modification between 2017 and 2025. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, stroke/transient ischaemic attack, and major bleeding.
RESULTS: A total of 55 patients were included (67% females). The median age was 78 years (interquartile range [IQR] 73-81); the median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality was 6.7% (IQR 4.8-9.5). AML modification was performed in 65.5% of cases with the Laceration of the Anterior Mitral leaflet to Prevent Outflow ObstructioN technique and in 34.5% with the Balloon-Assisted Translocation of the Mitral Anterior Leaflet technique. AML modification was successful in 96.4% of cases. Despite successful AML modification, haemodynamically significant LVOT obstruction occurred in 12.7% of cases. The co-primary in-hospital safety endpoint occurred in 20.0% of patients, driven by cardiovascular death in 14.5% of patients. Overall in-hospital mortality was 16.4%. The ViMAC substrate was associated with the numerically highest LVOT obstruction rate (ViMAC 20.7%, ViR 0.0%, ViV 8.3%, odds ratio [OR] 4.72, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.89-47.86; p=0.070). The aortomitral angle showed a borderline association with LVOT obstruction (OR 1.22 per degree, 95% CI: 0.99-1.48; p=0.059).
CONCLUSIONS: AML modification enables TMVR in high-risk anatomies with high feasibility but does not eliminate LVOT obstruction. ViMAC represents the most challenging substrate.

candidates.title: Bioprosthetic valve performance of transcatheter aortic valves.
candidates.abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is used increasingly in younger patients with longer life expectancy, necessitating long-term effectiveness. Randomised clinical trials have demonstrated comparable or superior haemodynamic performance of transcatheter heart valves (THVs) to surgical aortic valve replacement over midterm follow-up. Within a lifetime management framework, haemodynamic performance and durability of THVs are central considerations in patients undergoing aortic valve replacement for severe aortic stenosis. This review provides an overview of THV design and function along with contemporary clinical evidence, with a focus on current haemodynamic assessment considerations, challenges in cross-platform interpretation of valve performance, and limitations of randomised comparative evidence, as well as future directions in the evaluation of THV performance.

candidates.title: Transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement after failed edge-to-edge repair.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Residual or recurrent tricuspid regurgitation (TR) after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) is a growing concern in clinical practice and is associated with inferior outcomes.
AIMS: We sought to evaluate the early experience of transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR) in patients with failed TEER.
METHODS: This multicentre, retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing TTVR for recurrent or residual severe TR after TEER. Clinical, echocardiographic, and computed tomography findings were evaluated. The primary outcome was clinical success at 30 days after TTVR.
RESULTS: Of the 28 patients included (age 78.5±6.3 years, 61% female), 20 (72%) had residual TR and 8 (28%) had recurrent TR diagnosed within a median of 182 days after TEER. Patients were severely symptomatic (New York Heart Association [NYHA] III/IV in 97%), and 64% had massive/torrential TR. In 6 patients (21%), a commissural TEER device was evident, enabling direct TTVR (neocommissure strategy). Engagement of TEER devices with single leaflet device attachment during TTVR was carried out in 12 patients (43%), and electrosurgical laceration and stabilisation to facilitate TTVR in 10 patients (36%). Clinical success at 30 days was 93%. NYHA Functional Class improved in 93% of patients, with 85% being in NYHA I/II at 1 month after TTVR. Two patients died from non-cardiac reasons, and during a median follow-up of 69 days, 4 patients suffered a heart failure hospitalisation despite procedural success.
CONCLUSIONS: In this small patient cohort, three different TTVR strategies after failed TEER resulted in significant clinical success at 30 days and led to substantial symptom relief during short-term follow-up.

candidates.title: Acute right ventricular response to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Changes in right ventricular (RV) function are frequent after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), yet their mechanisms and prognostic implications remain incompletely defined.
AIMS: We sought to characterise acute RV functional changes following TTVR and evaluate their prognostic impact.
METHODS: This multicentre study included consecutive patients treated with TTVR between 2019 and 2025 with complete imaging data. RV function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline, intraprocedurally, and before discharge. RV end-systolic elastance (Ees), effective arterial elastance (Ea), and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive single-beat pressure-volume loop analysis. Changes over time were assessed using paired tests, and associations with mortality were investigated using Cox regression analysis with Firth's penalised likelihood.
RESULTS: Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years; 72% female; EVOQUE n=49; LuX-Valve Plus n=18) were included. At discharge, both cohorts showed declines in absolute RV free-wall longitudinal strain (aRV-FWLS; -10.4%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -10.4%; p=0.001 for LuX-Valve Plus) and fractional area change (FAC; -18.0%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -13.5%; p=0.005 for LuX-Valve Plus). Overall, 58% of patients met the criteria for severe RV dysfunction after TTVR. Over a median follow-up of 19 months, 15 patients died. Device type, acute RV functional changes, Ees, and Ees/Ea were not associated with mortality (allp>0.05). In contrast, computed tomography-derived RV coupling (hazard ratio [HR] 0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.89) and the coexistence of baseline longitudinal (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <17 mm and/or aRV-FWLS <23%) and circumferential (RV-FAC ≤35%) RV dysfunction (HR 3.93, 95% CI: 1.10-14.47) were associated with mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function. Although common, early postprocedural RV dysfunction was not associated with midterm mortality.

candidates.title: Outcomes of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement for Aortic Regurgitation in LVAD Patients: The JENA-VAD Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aortic regurgitation (AR) during left ventricular assist device (LVAD) support causes recurrent heart failure. Surgery is high risk and stenosis-designed valves anchor poorly in noncalcified anatomy.
OBJECTIVES: The goal of this study was to evaluate early outcomes of the AR-specific Trilogy transcatheter heart valve for LVAD-associated AR.
METHODS: JENA-VAD is a prospective, multicenter, single-arm investigational device exemption study. An independent committee adjudicated endpoints using VARC-3 (Valve Academic Research Consortium-3) definitions. The primary efficacy endpoint was the VARC-3 device success composite adapted for LVAD support, and the primary safety endpoint was the VARC-3 early safety composite.
RESULTS: Fifty patients were treated (mean age 69.2 years; 40% female). Median follow-up was 105 days (range 27 to 577 days). Technical and device success were 96.0% (95% CI: 86.3-99.5). Freedom from any component event of the VARC-3 early safety composite was 90.0% (95% CI: 78.2-96.7). At 30 days, 7 VARC-3 safety events occurred in 5 patients: type 2 to 4 bleeding (n = 2), major vascular complications (n = 2), device-related peripheral interventions (n = 2), and new pacemaker (1 of 7 without prior pacing; 14.3%). There were no strokes or myocardial infarctions. Two transient ischemic attacks occurred in patients without valve abnormalities. Beyond 30 days, cardiovascular death occurred in 1 patient (day 86). Follow-up computed tomography (CT) imaging or transesophageal echocardiography was obtained in 12 patients, and 11 (including 3 within 30 days) had leaflet thickening or thrombosis, including all patients who underwent CT. The remaining 38 patients did not have postprocedure imaging. Two of these events were symptomatic: valve thrombosis and a transient ischemic attack (day 116), and prosthetic AR that required valve-in-valve implantation (day 146) and subsequent heart transplantation. In exploratory analyses, NYHA functional class at 30 days was I or II in 72.3% (34 of 47) and Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score rose 11.5 ± 21.5 points (n = 44).
CONCLUSIONS: Transcatheter valve replacement using a dedicated system in LVAD patients was feasible with high technical and device success and without early death, stroke, or moderate or severe residual AR. Leaflet thickening or thrombosis, detected on clinically indicated CT imaging, occurred in 22%, representing a lower bound. Follow-up is ongoing to inform longer-term safety and effectiveness. (Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Using the JenaValve Trilogy Heart Valve System for Clinically Significant Aortic Regurgitation in Patients With Left Ventricular Assist Devices [LVAD]; NCT06594705).
