candidates.title: Early Implementation of Guideline-Directed Medical Therapy and Outcomes in Cardiogenic Shock Supported by Micro-Axial Flow Pumps.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The role of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in patients with cardiogenic shock (CS) supported by mechanical circulatory support remains poorly defined. The feasibility and potential benefits of early GDMT initiation during Impella support are uncertain.
METHODS: We analyzed a multicenter prospective registry of consecutive patients with CS treated with Impella between 2020 and 2024. GDMT exposure was defined as the number of heart failure therapies administered at device explantation. The primary outcome was in-hospital mortality. Multivariable logistic regression adjusted for clinical severity and early shock trajectory. Landmark analysis excluded patients dying within 5 days, while mixed-effects models accounted for center-level clustering.
RESULTS: Among 140 patients (mean age 61 years; 20% female), 40% received concomitant ECMO (ECPella). In-hospital mortality was 38%. At explantation, 43% received at least one GDMT agent. Greater GDMT exposure was independently associated with lower mortality (OR 0.28 per additional therapy; 95% CI 0.14-0.58; p<0.001). This association remained consistent in landmark analysis (adjusted OR 0.31; 95% CI 0.16-0.66; p<0.001) and after excluding patients with cardiac arrest (adjusted OR 0.48; 95% CI 0.23-0.88; p=0.002). A graded relationship between GDMT intensity and survival was observed. Center-level variability was negligible (intraclass correlation coefficient 0.02).
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with CS supported by Impella, early GDMT implementation was feasible in a substantial proportion of patients. Greater GDMT exposure at device explantation was associated with lower in-hospital mortality. Ventricular unloading may provide an opportunity to initiate outcome-modifying therapies during the acute phase of CS.

candidates.title: Impact of age on implementation and tolerability of guideline-directed medical therapy in patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Elderly patients constitute a growing proportion of patients with heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF), yet remain underrepresented in randomized clinical trials. We evaluated the impact of age on the implementation of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) in HFrEF.
METHODS: TITRATE-HF is a prospective, multicentre registry (enrolment June 2022-February 2024) including patients with de novo, chronic, and worsening heart failure (HF). For the current analysis, HFrEF patients were categorized by age (<65, 65-74, and ≥75 years). We assessed GDMT implementation, tolerability, and clinical outcomes (composite endpoint: first HF hospitalization or all-cause death).
RESULTS: The cohort included 980 patients aged <65 years (29%), 1120 patients aged 65-74 years (33%), and 1267 patients aged ≥75 years (38%). At 12-month follow-up, younger patients more frequently received GDMT, with quadruple therapy prescribed in 68% of those aged <65 years, 61% aged 65-74 years, and 51% aged ≥75 years (P < .001). In de novo HFrEF, age-related differences were observed within weeks after diagnosis, with faster and more extensive GDMT intensification in younger patients. Still, rates of treatment downgrades and the distribution of side effects were largely similar across age groups. Significant left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) improvement was observed in all age groups (all P < .001). The use of quadruple therapy at 6 months was associated with a lower risk of the composite endpoint between 6 and 12 months (adjusted hazard ratio 0.65, 95% confidence interval 0.50-0.86, P = .002), with consistent associations across age groups (P for interaction = .46).
CONCLUSIONS: Elderly patients with HFrEF received less intensive GDMT. Age-related differences emerged early after diagnosis, with fewer treatment intensifications in elderly patients but largely similar downgrade rates across age groups. These findings highlight the need for improved implementation strategies to optimize guideline-directed therapy and dosing levels in the ageing HFrEF population.

candidates.title: Temporal and Vessel-Specific Relationship Between Post-PCI Fractional Flow Reserve and Long-Term Clinical Outcomes.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Post-percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) fractional flow reserve (FFR) reflects residual physiological impairment after stent implantation and is a proven predictor of procedural success and prognosis. However, the temporal dynamics of its prognostic utility and its potential variation according to the target vessel remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to explore vessel-specific post-PCI FFR thresholds and evaluate their prognostic consistency over 5 years.
METHODS: We analyzed 2128 patients undergoing successful drug-eluting stent implantation from the international Post-PCI FFR Extended registry. Patients were stratified according to the target vessel: left anterior descending artery (LAD) versus non-LAD. The primary end point was 5-year target vessel failure, defined as a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction, or target vessel revascularization. Restricted cubic spline models were used to explore the continuous association between post-PCI FFR and target vessel failure and to identify vessel-specific risk thresholds. Temporal prognostic performance was assessed via 3-year landmark analysis and time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic curves.
RESULTS: During 5-year follow-up, target vessel failure occurred in 176 patients (11.7%) with LAD lesions and 74 patients (11.7%) with non-LAD lesions. Lower post-PCI FFR was independently associated with a higher risk of target vessel failure in both LAD and non-LAD vessels. Spline analyses characterized vessel-stratified risk patterns, and exploratory comparisons used post-PCI FFR cut points of 0.83 for LAD and 0.94 for non-LAD vessels. Landmark analysis indicated that the excess hazard associated with suboptimal FFR was predominantly concentrated within the first 3 years postprocedure. Nevertheless, time-dependent receiver-operating characteristic analysis demonstrated modest but stable discriminatory power of post-PCI FFR throughout the 5-year follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: Post-PCI FFR provides sustained 5-year prognostic insight, though the exploratory vessel-stratified cut points require external validation. Although the associated risk is highest in the early to mid-term period, predictive discrimination persists long-term. These findings advocate for vessel-specific interpretation of post-PCI physiology to refine risk stratification and patient management.

candidates.title: Purkinje-Targeted Catheter Ablation for Refractory Ventricular Fibrillation and Polymorphic Ventricular Tachycardia: A Systematic Review, Network Meta-Analysis, and Meta-Regression.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Ventricular fibrillation (VF) and polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PVT) are major causes of sudden cardiac death. Although Purkinje-targeted catheter ablation has emerged as a rescue therapy for refractory ventricular arrhythmias, the comparative safety and efficacy of trigger-focused ablation versus Purkinje de-networking (PDN) remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To synthesize clinical outcomes for Purkinje-targeted interventions across diverse arrhythmic phenotypes.
METHODS: We searched PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, Ovid, and CENTRAL for studies enrolling adults with recurrent or refractory ventricular fibrillation (VF) or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia (PVT). We performed pairwise and network meta-analyses using random-effects models. We evaluated the certainty of evidence using GRADE frameworks (PROSPERO: CRD420261423684).
RESULTS: We included 22 studies involving 959 patients. Among PDN cohorts, pooled mortality was 13.5% (n = 435; 16 cohorts; 95% CI: 9.0%-20.1%; I2 = 99.28%), acute success was 83.5% (n = 388; 14 cohorts; 95% CI: 78.9%-88.4%; I2 = 34.33%), and VF/PVT recurrence was 18.9% (n = 412; 15 cohorts; 95% CI: 15.7%-22.6%; I2 = 0%). Compared with standard ablation, PDN showed nonsignificant reductions in mortality (RR 0.672, 95% CI: 0.267-1.69; I2 = 0%) and recurrence (RR 0.820, 95% CI: 0.239-2.807; I2 = 70.33%). In the primary network meta-analysis, PDN ranked highest for acute success (SUCRA 86.27%) and freedom from recurrence (77.05%). However, in a sensitivity analysis of comparative trials (9 trials; n = 457), trigger-focused ablation ranked highest for acute success (SUCRA 88.08% vs. 51.52% for PDN). New-onset LBBB occurred in up to 20.8% after substrate-based PDN.
CONCLUSIONS: In this exploratory network meta-analysis, PDN ranked favorably for acute procedural success and short-term arrhythmia freedom. However, low-certainty evidence, imprecise estimates, and substantial clinical heterogeneity preclude definitive conclusions about its comparative efficacy. Large-scale randomized trials are needed to establish its clinical benefit.

candidates.title: Kangaroo mother care to reduce morbidity and mortality in low birthweight infants.
candidates.abstract:
RATIONALE: Kangaroo mother care (KMC) comprises three core components: prolonged skin-to-skin contact between infants and caregivers; support for exclusive breastfeeding; and early discharge with appropriate follow-up. It provides thermal regulation and stabilizes cardiorespiratory and feeding functions. For low birthweight infants, KMC provides a feasible, low-cost approach to care that promotes thermal regulation, stabilizes cardiorespiratory and feeding functions, and minimizes parent-infant separation. This review updates a Cochrane review first published in 2003, with subsequent updates in 2011, 2014, and 2016.
OBJECTIVES: To determine the benefits and harms of kangaroo mother care (KMC) in low birthweight infants as an alternative to conventional neonatal care before or after the initial period of stabilization with conventional care.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, LILACS, CINAHL and trials registries in August 2025. We checked reference lists of included studies, and systematic reviews where subject matter related to the intervention or population examined in this review.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: We included randomized controlled trials (RCTs) where participants were hospitalized preterm infants (defined as < 37 weeks' gestation) or low birthweight infants (defined as birthweight < 2500 g). We included studies that evaluated KMC, defined as skin-to-skin contact between caregiver and infant, regardless of duration ('any KMC'), as well as KMC meeting the World Health Organization (WHO) definition (minimum duration of eight hours per day). Eligible comparisons were: any KMC compared with conventional neonatal care (CNC).
OUTCOMES: Critical outcomes were: in-hospital mortality or before 40 to 41 weeks' postmenstrual age (PMA); weight (g) at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA; exclusive breastfeeding at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA; any breastfeeding at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA; length of hospital stay; nosocomial (hospital-acquired) infection or sepsis (as defined in individual studies) at any time point, and hypothermia (as defined in individual studies) at any time point.
RISK OF BIAS: We used the Cochrane Risk of bias tool 2.0 (RoB 2).
SYNTHESIS METHODS: We conducted meta-analyses using fixed-effect models to calculate risk ratios (RR) and risk difference (RD) for dichotomous data, and mean differences (MDs) for continuous data, with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). We evaluated the certainty of evidence using GRADE.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 49 RCTs enrolling 7724 infants. Studies were published between 1988 and 2024. All studies compared any KMC with CNC; 13 delivered WHO-defined KMC for 8 to 24 hours/day, while the remainder offered KMC for different durations. Thus, the 'any KMC' comparison encompasses a range of exposure durations, not solely the WHO-defined intervention. Twenty-two studies were conducted in low- or middle-income countries. We identified eight ongoing studies.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Any KMC likely reduces in-hospital mortality or before 40 to 41 weeks' PMA (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.67 to 0.99; I² = 0%; 14 studies, 4389 participants; moderate-certainty evidence; RD -0.01, 95% CI -0.02 to 0.00, I2 = 0%) and nosocomial infection or sepsis (as defined in individual studies) (RR 0.66, 95% CI 0.54 to 0.82; I² = 45%; 15 studies, 3852 participants; moderate-certainty evidence; RD -0.03, 95% CI -0.05 to -0.02, I2 = 75%) compared to CNC. KMC may increase exclusive breastfeeding (RR 1.18, 95% CI 1.10 to 1.27; I² = 58%; 9 studies, 1846 participants; low-certainty evidence; RD 0.10, 95% CI 0.06 to 0.14, I2 = 73%) and reduce hypothermia (as defined in individual studies) at any time point (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.78 to 0.86; I² = 87%; 13 studies, 3493 participants; low-certainty evidence; RD -0.11, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.09, I2 = 93%). The evidence is very uncertain about the effect of any KMC on weight (g) at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA (MD 63.00, 95% CI 40.57 to 85.43; I² = 80%; 7 studies, 1648 participants; very low-certainty evidence), any breastfeeding at discharge or at 40 to 41 weeks' PMA (RR 1.10, 95% CI 1.00 to 1.21; I² = 68%; 6 studies, 1282 participants; very low-certainty evidence), and length of hospital stay (days) (MD 1.19, 95% CI 1.18 to 1.21; I² = 98%; 14 studies, 3765 participants; very low-certainty evidence). Subgroup analyses suggested differences in some outcomes by KMC definition and country income, but these findings require cautious interpretation. Certainty of the evidence varies from moderate for mortality and nosocomial infection or sepsis, low for exclusive breastfeeding and hypothermia, and very low for weight, any breastfeeding and length of hospital stay. Downgrading reflected risk of bias (unclear allocation concealment, unblinded outcome assessment, maternal-reported breastfeeding outcomes), inconsistency from heterogeneity and variable outcome definitions, indirectness from heterogeneous KMC delivery, and imprecision.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: KMC probably provides clinically important benefits compared with CNC, particularly by reducing mortality and nosocomial infection or sepsis. It may also improve breastfeeding outcomes and reduce hypothermia. Effects on growth and duration of hospitalization remain very uncertain because of substantial heterogeneity and very low-certainty evidence. Evidence for mortality and infection came predominantly from low- and lower-middle-income countries, with limited and imprecise evidence from high-income settings, restricting conclusions about applicability across settings. These conclusions apply to a broad definition of KMC; only a minority of trials evaluated KMC that met the WHO duration criterion, so the pooled results should not be taken as specific estimates of WHO-defined KMC. Future research should prioritize how KMC can be delivered effectively across health systems, income settings, and infant populations, including contemporary high-income neonatal care settings. Studies should clearly describe intervention components, including whether KMC meets the WHO definition, timing of initiation, daily duration, continuity, setting, provider, and implementation fidelity. Adequately powered trials and implementation studies should use standardized outcome definitions and address outcomes for which evidence remains very uncertain, including growth, hypothermia, and duration of hospitalization. Longer-term follow-up should assess mortality, neurodevelopment, breastfeeding, growth, family-centred outcomes, adverse effects, resource use, cost-effectiveness, equity, and feasibility.
FUNDING: None.
REGISTRATION: Original review (2003): doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002771 Last review update (2016): doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD002771.pub4.

candidates.title: Acupoint Thread Embedding for Weight Loss in Women With Overweight or Obesity : A Randomized Controlled Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Whether acupoint thread embedding (ATE), a traditional Chinese medicine intervention, produces weight reduction remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVE: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of ATE for weight reduction in women with overweight or obesity.
DESIGN: Randomized, sham-controlled trial masked to participants, outcome assessors, and analysts. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT06316310).
SETTING: Acupuncture Department, Shanghai Municipal Hospital of Traditional Chinese Medicine, Shanghai, China.
PARTICIPANTS: 132 women aged 18 to 45 years with a body mass index (BMI) of 24.0 kg/m2 or greater.
INTERVENTION: Participants were randomly assigned 1:1 to ATE (6 sessions over 12 weeks) or sham ATE (superficial needle insertion at the same acupoints without manipulation, de qi, thread placement, or needle retention), followed by a 12-week follow-up.
MEASUREMENTS: The primary outcome was change in BMI from baseline to week 12, analyzed under the intention-to-treat principle using linear mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: At week 12, BMI and body weight decreased 0.7 kg/m2 (95% CI, -1.0 to -0.3 kg/m2) and 1.8 kg (CI, -2.7 to -0.9 kg), respectively, more with ATE than with sham ATE; at week 24, differences were -1.1 kg/m2 (CI, -1.7 to -0.6 kg/m2) and -3.0 kg (CI, -4.5 to -1.6 kg), respectively. Weight reduction of 5% or more occurred in 25.8% versus 9.1% (risk difference, 16.7 percentage points [CI, 3.7 to 29.3 percentage points]) at 12 weeks. Acupoint thread embedding produced greater reductions in waist and hip circumference, body fat percentage, and appetite scores, whereas cardiometabolic and patient-reported outcomes did not differ. Adverse events were mild and comparably distributed.
LIMITATION: Single center, generally healthy women of reproductive age, unmasked acupuncturists, short-term follow-up, and underpowered for uncommon adverse events and subgroup analyses.
CONCLUSION: Acupoint thread embedding produced modest but sustained reductions in BMI and adiposity-related measures in Chinese women of reproductive age with overweight or obesity.

candidates.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Symptomatic Nonobstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy: Initial Clinical Experience.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Nonobstructive hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (nHCM), defined as hypertrophic cardiomyopathy without left ventricular outflow tract obstruction, remains challenging to treat because of its heterogeneous pathophysiology. This study evaluated the safety and efficacy of transapical beating-heart septal myectomy in patients with symptomatic nHCM.
METHODS: Patients with symptomatic, drug-refractory nHCM were prospectively enrolled to undergo transapical beating-heart septal myectomy through a left minithoracotomy. Under real-time transesophageal echocardiographic guidance, septal myectomy was tailored to relieve systolic cavity obliteration and mid-to-apical ventricular obstruction and to enlarge the left ventricular cavity. The primary end point was procedural success at 6 to 12 months postoperatively, defined as fulfillment of all prespecified criteria compared with baseline: ≥1-class improvement in New York Heart Association functional class, ≥10-point increase in Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score, ≥10-mL increase in stroke volume, and normal or grade I diastolic function.
RESULTS: Between January 2023 and January 2025, 97 consecutive eligible patients with nHCM underwent transapical beating-heart septal myectomy at Tongji Hospital. At postoperative 6 to 12 months, procedural success was achieved in 87.6%. Specifically, New York Heart Association functional class I increased from 0% at baseline to 93.8% at follow-up, the median Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire score improved from 64 (interquartile range, 56-69) to 87 (interquartile range, 82-92; P<0.001), the stroke volume increased from 53.5 mL (interquartile range, 41.0-66.6 mL) to 70.8 mL (interquartile range, 61.3-82.3 mL; P<0.001), and normal or grade I diastolic function increased from 65.6% to 97.9%. Among patients who underwent paired cardiopulmonary exercise testing (n=58), peak oxygen uptake increased by 1.1±2.9 mL/kg/min (P=0.008). In an exploratory, hypothesis-generating analysis of 12 patients with paired 13N-ammonia positron emission tomography, coronary flow reserve increased from 1.8±0.3 to 2.0±0.4 (P=0.034). Adverse events included mitral valve injury (n=1) and ventricular septal perforation (n=1), the latter resulting in 1 postoperative death.
CONCLUSIONS: Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy was associated with favorable left ventricular geometric remodeling and meaningful improvements in symptoms, health status, and functional capacity in selected patients with symptomatic nHCM. Being a potential therapeutic option for a previously difficult-to-treat population, it warrants further evaluation in controlled, multicenter studies.

candidates.title: Biatrial Versus Left Atrial Maze Ablation During Cardiac Valve Surgery for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The ABLATION Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines recommend concomitant surgical ablation during cardiac surgery in patients with atrial fibrillation (AF). However, the optimal lesion set remains uncertain, with ongoing debate regarding the relative benefits and risks of biatrial versus left atrial (LA) maze ablation.
METHODS: In this multicenter, randomized, single-blind trial, patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic mitral valve surgery, with or without concomitant cardiac surgical procedures, were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo biatrial or LA maze ablation. The biatrial group underwent a complete Cox-Maze IV procedure; the LA group received a left-sided maze lesion set. To ensure standardization and consistency of the ablation procedures, surgeons underwent pretrial training and certification, and all procedures were videorecorded and centrally reviewed. The primary outcome was freedom from atrial tachyarrhythmias lasting >30 seconds without antiarrhythmic drugs within 12 months. The key secondary end point was freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation.
RESULTS: All 323 randomized patients were included in the intention-to-treat analysis (mean age, 56.5 years; 72.1% women; mean LA diameter, 51.9 mm). At 12 months, 78.7% of patients (129 of 164) in the biatrial group and 68.6% (109 of 159) in the LA group were free from atrial tachyarrhythmias (adjusted difference, 10.7% [1-sided lower 95% CI, 3%]; P=0.01). Freedom from permanent pacemaker implantation was noted in 97.0% (159 of 164) of the biatrial group and 98.1% (156 of 159) of the LA group, meeting the predefined noninferiority criterion with a margin of -5% (adjusted difference, -1.1% [1-sided lower 95% CI, -3.9%]; Pnoninferiority=0.01).
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with persistent or long-standing persistent AF undergoing rheumatic cardiac valve surgery, biatrial maze ablation was superior to LA maze ablation in reducing recurrent atrial tachyarrhythmias, while maintaining noninferiority with respect to permanent pacemaker implantation. These findings provide direct evidence to inform lesion-set selection for surgical ablation during cardiac surgery.

candidates.title: Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation: From Prolapse to Precision Therapy.
candidates.abstract: Degenerative mitral valve regurgitation due to mitral valve prolapse affects ≈15 million people globally and is the commonest indication for mitral intervention in high-income countries, but its biology, natural history, and lifetime management are ill defined. This review summarizes current knowledge of the epidemiology, pathophysiology, diagnosis, risk stratification, and lifetime management of degenerative mitral regurgitation, with a focus on areas of uncertainty, recent advances, and emerging research directions. These include translational research focused on determining genetic and cellular drivers of disease progression and mechanistic studies geared to improve detection and prevention of downstream myocardial dysfunction, particularly in high-risk phenotypes, including arrhythmic mitral prolapse. The current landscape of randomized trials and large registries comparing contemporary surgical and transcatheter treatment and strategies to improve patient access to care and outcomes across all patient risk profiles and populations are also discussed.

candidates.title: Transapical Beating-Heart Septal Myectomy for Obstructive Hypertrophic Cardiomyopathy.
candidates.abstract: Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) is a prevalent heterogenous genetic cardiac disorder. In the cardiac myosin inhibitor era, the guideline-directed management of HCM remains an emerging frontier worldwide. Septal myectomy has been the gold standard treatment option for obstructive HCM over the past 60 years. However, the complexity of this procedure and required expertise (and lack of qualified training) have limited its success and availability beyond high-volume HCM centers. Transapical beating-heart septal myectomy (TA-BSM), a newly developed innovative technique, simplifies conventional septal myectomy by eliminating the need for sternotomy, cardiopulmonary bypass, and aortotomy. Most important, the inclusion of real-time intraoperative echocardiographic guidance and evaluation makes TA-BSM safer, more precise, cost-effective, and reproducible. The apparent advantages of TA-BSM, including substantial reductions in surgical trauma and operating times and much faster postoperative recovery in patients with obstructive HCM, are encouraging. TA-BSM is particularly feasible in patients with long-segment obstruction, or small aortic valve annulus, or in those who had undergone previous cardiac operations. The frequent resolution of systolic anterior motion and associated mitral regurgitation after TA-BSM, without concomitant mitral valve intervention, highlights the central role of intraoperative echocardiography and close surgeon-echocardiographer collaboration in achieving optimal procedural outcomes. Further multicenter evaluation of TA-BSM will help define its role among septal reduction strategies for patients with obstructive HCM.

candidates.title: 10-Year Outcomes of Initial CTO-PCI vs No CTO-PCI Strategies for Chronic Total Occlusion: The DECISION-CTO Randomized Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: The long-term clinical effects of percutaneous coronary intervention for chronic total occlusion (CTO-PCI) remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to compare 10-year clinical outcomes between initial CTO-PCI and no CTO-PCI strategies in the extended follow-up of the DECISION-CTO trial.
METHODS: The DECISION-CTO trial was an open-label, multicenter, randomized trial conducted at 19 centers in 5 Asian countries. Patients were randomly assigned to an initial strategy of CTO-PCI or no CTO-PCI, with guideline-directed medical therapy in both groups and PCI of obstructive non-CTO lesions encouraged in both groups. The primary endpoint was a composite of death from any cause, myocardial infarction, stroke, or any revascularization at 10 years, analyzed in the modified intention-to-treat group.
RESULTS: Between March 2010 and October 2016, 834 patients were randomly assigned, and 804 of these patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (413 CTO-PCI, 391 no CTO-PCI). Clinical follow-up at 10 years was complete in 688 patients (85.6%), without a significant between-group difference (P = 0.69). At 10 years, the primary endpoint had occurred in 134 patients in the CTO-PCI group and 138 patients in the no CTO-PCI group (Kaplan-Meier estimates: 33.9% vs 37.4%; risk difference: -3.5 percentage points; 95% CI: -10.4 to 3.3 percentage points; P = 0.32). Restricted mean event-free survival time at 10 years was also similar between groups (7.52 vs 7.53 years; difference: -0.01 years; 95% CI: -0.54 to 0.52 years; P = 0.97). Death from any cause did not differ significantly between groups (12.7% vs 16.5%; HR: 0.76; 95% CI: 0.52-1.12; P = 0.16).
CONCLUSIONS: Over 10 years, an initial strategy of CTO-PCI was not associated with a significant difference in the primary endpoint or all-cause mortality compared with an initial strategy of no CTO-PCI. However, the wide CIs preclude definitive conclusions regarding the potential benefit or harm of an initial CTO-PCI strategy. (Drug-Eluting Stent Implantation Versus Optimal Medical Treatment in Patients With Chronic Total Occlusion [DECISION-CTO]; NCT01078051; extended follow-up, NCT06908499).

candidates.title: Low-dose oral misoprostol for induction of labour.
candidates.abstract:
RATIONALE: Oral misoprostol is a common labour induction method. This review is restricted to lower doses (initially ≤ 50 µg), as higher doses pose unacceptably high risks of uterine hyperstimulation.
OBJECTIVES: To assess the benefits and harms of low-dose oral misoprostol for labour induction in women with a viable fetus in the third trimester of pregnancy, compared with other methods of labour induction.
SEARCH METHODS: We searched CENTRAL, MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, ClinicalTrials.gov and the WHO ICTRP, and checked reference lists of retrieved studies. The search date was April 2025.
ELIGIBILITY CRITERIA: Randomised trials comparing low-dose oral misoprostol (≤ 50 µg initial dose) versus placebo, vaginal dinoprostone, vaginal misoprostol, oxytocin or mechanical methods, or comparing oral protocols (20 µg hourly titrated versus 25 µg two-hourly static; 20 µg to 25 µg versus 50 µg or one- to two-hourly versus four- to six-hourly).
OUTCOMES: Our critical outcomes were vaginal birth within 24 hours, caesarean section and uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes.
RISK OF BIAS: We assessed the risk of bias using RoB 1.
SYNTHESIS METHODS: Two authors independently screened reports, extracted data and assessed risk of bias. We synthesised results using random-effects meta-analysis, expressing effect estimates as risk ratios (RR) or mean differences (MD) and assessing heterogeneity using I². We evaluated evidence certainty using GRADE.
INCLUDED STUDIES: We included 44 trials (38 from the previous version, 6 new), involving 11,795 women.
SYNTHESIS OF RESULTS: Oral misoprostol versus placebo/no treatment (3 trials, 294 women) Vaginal birth within 24 hours was not reported. Oral misoprostol probably results in little or no difference in caesarean section (RR 0.73, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.48 to 1.11; 3 trials, 294 women; moderate-certainty evidence); its effect on uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes is uncertain (RR 5.15, 95% CI 0.25 to 105.31; 2 trials, 195 women; low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus vaginal dinoprostone (9 trials, 3188 women) Oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours compared with vaginal dinoprostone, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 0.94, 95% CI 0.84 to 1.05; 6 trials, 2492 women; very low-certainty evidence). It may also result in little or no difference in caesarean section (RR 0.91, 95% CI 0.80 to 1.04; 9 trials, 3185 women; low-certainty evidence) and in uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 0.89, 95% CI 0.59 to 1.33; 7 trials, 2593 women; low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus vaginal misoprostol (20 trials, 4130 women) Oral misoprostol may result in fewer vaginal births within 24 hours (RR 0.78, 95% CI 0.63 to 0.97; 11 trials, 2771 women; low-certainty evidence), may result in little or no difference in caesarean section (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.76 to 1.07; 20 trials, 4128 women; low-certainty evidence) and may result in less uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 0.70, 95% CI 0.52 to 0.95; 16 trials, 3431 women; low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus intravenous oxytocin (4 trials, 426 women) Oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 1.04, 95% CI 0.90 to 1.21; 2 trials, 210 women; very low-certainty evidence), in caesarean section (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.58 to 1.30; 4 trials, 426 women; low-certainty evidence) and in uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 0.72, 95% CI 0.17 to 3.08; 2 trials, 248 women; very low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol versus mechanical methods (9 trials, 3794 women) Oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 1.41, 95% CI 0.97 to 2.05; 5 trials, 1273 women; very low-certainty evidence), probably reduces caesarean section (RR 0.85, 95% CI 0.76 to 0.95; 9 trials, 3746 women; moderate-certainty evidence) and probably increases uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes (RR 1.60, 95% CI 1.01 to 2.54; 6 trials, 3275 women; moderate-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol 20 µg hourly titrated versus 25 µg two-hourly static (1 trial, 146 women) Oral misoprostol 20 µg hourly titrated may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours compared with oral misoprostol 25 µg two-hourly static, but the evidence is very uncertain (RR 0.98, 95% CI 0.77 to 1.24; 1 trial, 146 women; very low-certainty evidence) and may increase caesarean section (RR 2.83, 95% CI 1.18 to 6.78; 1 trial, 146 women; low-certainty evidence); its effect on uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes is uncertain (RR 3.00, 95% CI 0.12 to 72.45; 1 trial, 146 women; very low-certainty evidence). Oral misoprostol 20 µg to 25 µg versus 50 µg (1 trial, 64 women) The use of 20 µg to 25 µg versus 50 µg of oral misoprostol may result in little to no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours (RR 0.60, 95% CI 0.31 to 1.17; 1 trial, 64 women; very low-certainty evidence) or in caesarean section (RR 1.31, 95% CI 0.77 to 2.22; 1 trial, 64 women; very low-certainty evidence) but the evidence is very uncertain; no cases of uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes were reported. Oral misoprostol one- to two-hourly versus four- to six-hourly (1 trial; 64 women) This comparison is based on the same single trial as the previous comparison, and the findings are therefore identical.
AUTHORS' CONCLUSIONS: Low-dose oral misoprostol has similar effects to other commonly used induction methods across most key outcomes. Certainty of the evidence ranged from very low to moderate, mainly due to imprecision and inconsistency. Compared with placebo, vaginal dinoprostone and intravenous oxytocin, oral misoprostol may result in little or no difference in vaginal birth within 24 hours or caesarean section. Compared with vaginal misoprostol, oral misoprostol may reduce uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes, but may also reduce vaginal births within 24 hours. Compared with mechanical methods, oral misoprostol probably reduces caesarean section, although it probably increases uterine hyperstimulation with fetal heart rate changes.
FUNDING: This Cochrane review had no dedicated funding.

candidates.title: Myocardial Work Analysis: A Novel Echocardiographic Approach for Early Detection of Myocardial Fibrosis in Pediatric Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy With Preserved LVEF-A Prospective Cohort Study.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: While myocardial work (MW) indices have shown diagnostic and prognostic value in various cardiovascular diseases, their role in detecting myocardial fibrosis in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) remains unexplored. This prospective study investigates MW's potential for early identification of fibrosis in pediatric DMD patients with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction.
METHODS: In this large prospective cohort, we enrolled 242 genetically confirmed DMD males (aged 6-18 years) with left ventricular ejection fraction ≥50% by cardiac magnetic resonance and 54 age-matched controls. Comprehensive echocardiographic assessment included global work index, global constructive work, global wasted work, and global work efficiency analysis. Myocardial fibrosis was assessed via late gadolinium enhancement on cardiac magnetic resonance at baseline at 1-year follow-up.
RESULTS: Patients with DMD demonstrated significantly impaired MW indices versus controls (global work index, 1371.4±225.84 versus 1598.04±207.01 mm Hg%; global work efficiency, median 94.67% [Q1-Q3, 93.00-96.00] versus 95.33% [94.30-96.33]; global constructive work, 1630.34±246.37 versus 1900.22±195.84 mm Hg%; global wasted work, median 67.67 [Q1-Q3, 50.17-86.25] versus 59.00 [48.00-73.00] mm Hg%; all P<0.01). Notably, MW abnormalities preceded global longitudinal strain reduction, with significant differences even in patients with DMD with normal global longitudinal strain (≥18%). Global work efficiency showed moderate diagnostic accuracy for baseline late gadolinium enhancement (area under the curve, 0.618) and was associated with subsequent late gadolinium enhancement development in exploratory longitudinal analysis (area under the curve, 0.798; cutoff of 95.85%), providing complementary information beyond conventional echocardiographic parameters.
CONCLUSIONS: This large-scale prospective study suggests that MW analysis, particularly global work efficiency, might be useful for early detection of cardiac dysfunction and might be associated with short-term fibrosis in patients with DMD and preserved left ventricular ejection fraction. However, given the limited number of progression events, this finding should be interpreted cautiously.

candidates.title: Early Left Bundle Branch Pacing for Complete Left Bundle Branch Block and Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction of 36%-50%: The EARLY-RESYNC Randomized Trial.
candidates.abstract:
AIMS: To compare the effects of early resynchronization with left bundle branch pacing (early-LBBP) versus guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT) alone on cardiac function in patients with complete left bundle branch block (CLBBB) and left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of 36%-50%.
METHODS AND RESULTS: In this prospective, randomized, multicenter trial, 37 patients (mean age 60.5 ± 12.3 years, male 40.5%, LVEF 42.6% ± 6.0%) were assigned to early-LBBP plus GDMT (n=19) or GDMT alone (n=18). The primary endpoint was the between-group difference in the change of LVEF from baseline to 6 months. Secondary endpoints included changes in echocardiographic parameters and clinical outcomes. Analyses were performed according to the intention-to-treat principle. At 6-month follow-up, the adjusted mean improvement in LVEF was greater in the early-LBBP group than in the GDMT group (mean difference: 7.4%, 95% CI: 1.9 to 12.9%; P =0.013), with consistent findings in the per-protocol analysis. Early-LBBP was also associated with a greater reduction in LV end-systolic volume (-23.6mL; 95% CI: -42.3 to -4.8ml) and a higher rate of final LVEF ≥50% (78.9% vs. 38.9%) at 6 months compared with GDMT alone.
CONCLUSION: In patients with CLBBB and LVEF 36%-50%, LBBP combined with GDMT resulted in greater improvement in LVEF at 6 months than GDMT alone. Larger randomized trials are needed to establish its long-term clinical benefits and optimal timing.

candidates.title: Sex differences in mechanical circulatory support efficacy in infarct-related cardiogenic shock. An individual patient data meta-analysis.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Routine use of active mechanical circulatory support (MCS) in infarct-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) remains controversial. Although recent evidence suggests potential benefit in selected patients, the influence of sex on MCS efficacy is poorly defined.
AIMS: To evaluate whether sex modifies the effect of MCS in AMI-CS.
METHODS: Randomized trials comparing early routine MCS with standard care in AMI-CS and reporting 6-month mortality were identified through January 2025. Individual patient data were analyzed using study-stratified Cox models. The primary outcome was 6-month all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included 30-day mortality, major bleeding, and peripheral ischemic vascular complications.
RESULTS: Nine trials including 213 (20%) female and 845 male patients were analysed. Women were older than men (67.6 vs. 63.7 years; P < 0.001) and had higher 6-month mortality (60% vs. 52%; P = 0.03). Early routine MCS was not associated with significantly lower mortality in either women (HR, 0.99; 95% CI, 0.70-1.42) or men (HR, 0.84; 95% CI, 0.70-1.02; P for interaction = 0.41). Among DanGer Shock-like patients, MCS was associated with lower mortality in men (HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.51-0.86), but not in women (HR, 1.18; 95% CI, 0.72-1.91; P for interaction = 0.02). MCS increased complications in both sexes.
CONCLUSIONS: Women with AMI-CS were underrepresented and had higher mortality than men. No sex-specific treatment effect was observed overall, whereas subgroup findings suggested possible heterogeneity in DanGer-Shock-like patients. These findings, limited by small number of female patients and wide confidence intervals, support the need for adequately powered trials with sufficient female representation.

candidates.title: Angiography-Derived vs Wire-Based Fractional Flow Reserve to Guide Revascularization: The Randomized LIPSIA-STRATEGY Trial.
candidates.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Wire-based physiological assessment is recommended to guide coronary revascularization but remains underused. Angiography-derived physiology offers a wire-free alternative; however, randomized comparisons with pressure wire fractional flow reserve (FFR) have yielded inconsistent findings.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to determine whether angiography-derived vessel fractional flow reserve (vFFR)-guided revascularization is noninferior to pressure wire FFR guidance for intermediate coronary stenoses.
METHODS: The multicenter, investigator-initiated, randomized LIPSIA-STRATEGY trial included patients with acute or chronic coronary syndromes and at least 1 intermediate coronary stenosis at 8 German centers. Patients were randomized 1:1 to undergo revascularization based on vFFR or FFR. The primary outcome was major adverse cardiac events, defined as a composite of cardiac death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, or unplanned clinically driven revascularization within 1 year, analyzed by modified intention to treat against a noninferiority margin of 3.5 percentage points.
RESULTS: Between June 2020 and February 2025, 1,053 patients (median age: 69 years) underwent randomization (vFFR, n = 528; FFR, n = 525). At 1 year, major adverse cardiac events occurred in 15 of 493 patients (3.0%) in the vFFR group and in 20 of 493 (4.1%) in the FFR group (risk difference: -1.01 percentage points; P for noninferiority <0.001); the primary outcome was ascertainable in 986 of the 1,053 randomized patients. The upper boundary of the 1-sided 97.5% CI for the risk difference was 1.29 percentage points, below the prespecified margin (relative risk: 0.75; 95% CI: 0.39-1.45). Physiological values of 0.80 or less occurred in 43.1% vs 35.9% of patients, and the study lesion was revascularized in 41.2% vs 35.5%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients with intermediate coronary stenoses requiring physiological assessment, a vFFR-guided revascularization strategy met the prespecified absolute criterion for noninferiority to wire-based FFR at 1 year. Because the observed event rate was lower than anticipated, the margin was less conservative on a relative scale than intended. In a post hoc sensitivity analysis using the relative margin of 1.44 implied by the original assumptions, noninferiority was not met in the primary modified intention-to-treat population. In the corresponding post hoc per-protocol sensitivity analysis, noninferiority was met using this relative margin. Whether that additional revascularization is beneficial is not answered by similar 1-year event rates. (Comparison of Vessel-FFR Versus FFR in Intermediate Coronary Stenoses; NCT03497637; Protocol ID HRC045277.).

candidates.title: Alcohol and cardiovascular disease: inter-organ crosstalk, microvascular dysfunction, and cardiovascular ageing.
candidates.abstract: Alcohol-related cardiovascular risk is being fundamentally reappraised. Observational associations suggesting cardioprotection with light-to-moderate drinking have been challenged by contemporary cohort analyses, Mendelian-randomization studies, biomarker-informed investigations, and updated public-health guidance. Uncertainty nevertheless persists at very low exposure levels and for selected coronary or all-cause outcomes. Alcohol is therefore best viewed as a dose-, pattern-, and host-dependent cardiovascular stressor. Acute or binge drinking, sustained heavy intake, chronic intake with episodic binges, and withdrawal produce overlapping but distinct phenotypes, including hypertension, atrial fibrillation, ventricular arrhythmias, sudden death, alcohol-associated cardiomyopathy, heart failure, stroke, and vascular disease. A systems-cardiology framework is presented in which direct myocardial injury, electrical instability, haemodynamic and autonomic stress, vascular and microvascular dysfunction, and disrupted inter-organ signalling interact. Ethanol and acetaldehyde toxicity, redox imbalance, microbial and inflammatory mediators, neurohumoral activation, and metabolic or electrolyte disturbances can impair endothelial signalling, mitochondrial energetics, excitation-contraction coupling, electrical stability, and repair. Pathway dominance varies across exposure patterns and susceptible hosts; coronary microvascular dysfunction may represent a convergence pathway rather than an obligatory mediator. Cumulative injury can diminish perfusion, contractile, electrical, autonomic, and exercise reserve. Alcohol-related cardiovascular ageing is proposed as a unifying cumulative phenotype encompassing mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative and nitrative stress, inflammageing, senescence, impaired repair, circadian and epigenetic dysregulation, fibrosis, and ventriculo-arterial uncoupling, although direct human evidence remains incomplete. Age, biological sex, genetics, comorbidities, sleep-circadian disruption, nutrition, medications, and polysubstance misuse may modify pathway dominance and reversibility. Structured exposure assessment and alcohol reduction or abstinence, when indicated, are actionable components of cardiovascular prevention and care.
